definition_zh: 意见；看法；评价；舆论
definition_en: what a person thinks about something, a judgement offered as advice, or the body of views held by many people
core_image: 一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿
scene: 夏夜的阳台上，两个人靠着栏杆聊到很晚，一个说出自己的判断，另一个只是听着，没有立刻反驳。In her opinion, the plan needs more time before it can work.
sceneCN: 这里的 opinion 是「看法、意见」（第 1 个义项：个人对事情的判断）；句意为依她看，这个方案还需要更多时间才能奏效。图中可辨识物件：阳台栏杆、写字的纸片。

collocations.zh: 看法问题；见仁见智的事

derivatives.zh: 由 opinion 加 -ated 构成，义为「固执己见的；自负的」
由 opinionated 加 -ness 构成，义为「固执己见的性情」
由 opinion 与 poll 复合而成，义为「民意调查」

senses.title: What a person thinks about something
senses.definition: a belief or judgement that a person forms about a matter, without claiming it is a proven fact
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某事形成的看法或判断，并不宣称它已被证实为事实
senses.example: In my opinion, the meeting could have been shorter.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这次会议本可以开得更短。
senses.why: The Latin verb opinari meant to think or suppose, so the noun starts as the act of holding a view in one's mind rather than as knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为「以为、揣度」，所以这个名词的起点是心里抱着一种看法，而不是已经掌握的知识。

senses.title: A judgement given as advice
senses.definition: a considered view offered by someone whose knowledge is being asked for, as in a second opinion
senses.definitionCN: 由具备相关知识的人给出、供人参考的判断，如另请人再作一次评估
senses.example: The doctor suggested she get a second opinion before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议她在手术前再找一位同行评估。
senses.why: Once a view is worth consulting, the word shifts from private belief to a judgement that carries a specialist's weight.
senses.whyCN: 一种看法一旦值得专门请教，这个词便从私人的信念转成带有专业分量的判断。

senses.title: The views held by many people together
senses.definition: the general body of views held by the public at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期公众整体所持的各种看法
senses.example: Public opinion turned against the new tax within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 不到一个月，公众舆论就转而反对这项新税。
senses.why: Many private views, counted together, become a force of their own, and English lets the same word name that collective weight.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人的看法汇在一起，就成了独立的力量，英语便用同一个词来指这份集体的分量。

senses.title: A point on which people differ
senses.titleCN: 看法问题；见仁见智的事
senses.definition: a matter that cannot be settled by evidence alone because it depends on how people judge it
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭证据无法定论、要靠各人如何判断的事情
senses.example: Whether the film is funny is a matter of opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影好不好笑，是个见仁见智的问题。
senses.why: If a view is not proof, then some questions cannot be closed by facts, and the word marks that limit openly.
senses.whyCN: 既然看法不等于证据，那么有些问题就无法靠事实了结，这个词恰好在提醒这条界线。

intro.en: Opinion came to English from Latin through French, and it began as a verb of thinking rather than a noun of belief; the family keeps that sense of judging without proof.
intro.cn: opinion 经法语由拉丁语进入英语，起初来自表示「思考」的动词而非表示「信念」的名词；这一族词始终保留「无确证而判断」的意味。

items.en: Opinari meant to think, suppose or believe, and it described the mind taking a position before certainty was reached.
items.cn: opinari 意为思考、揣度、相信，描写头脑在尚未确定之前先站到一个位置上。

items.en: The noun opinio grew from that verb and named a belief held in the mind, often in contrast with knowledge or proof.
items.cn: 名词 opinio 由该动词生长出来，指心中所抱的看法，常与知识或证据相对照。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opinion, meaning what one thinks or what people generally think, and it entered English with both readings.
items.cn: 古法语以 opinion 承袭该名词，既指个人所想，也指众人所想，进入英语时两种读法都在。

items.en: Middle English used opinion for personal views, for expert judgements and for the general voice of the people.
items.cn: 中古英语把 opinion 用于个人看法、专家判断，以及民众的一般声音。

items.en: Modern English keeps opinion for stated beliefs, for consulted advice and for public sentiment, and adds fixed phrases such as in my opinion and a matter of opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opinion 兼指说出的信念、请教得来的意见与公众情绪，并固定下 in my opinion、a matter of opinion 之类的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of thinking and judging; the near-meaning group collects other names for a view held about something.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「思考、判断」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示对某事所持看法的名称。

entries.definition: To state a view, often in a formal or slightly stiff tone.
entries.definitionCN: 说出看法，常带正式或略生硬的语气。

entries.definition: Holding views too firmly and unwilling to listen.
entries.definitionCN: 过于坚持己见、不肯听别人的。

entries.definition: Open to debate because no proof can settle it.
entries.definitionCN: 因无证据可定论而可以争论的。

entries.definition: The way a person sees or regards a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看待某事的眼光或角度。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true, often without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 常指未经证明而被当作真实接受的东西。

entries.definition: A decision reached after weighing the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡事实之后作出的判断。

entries.definition: A settled position taken toward an issue.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一问题所采取的既定立场。

normalIntro.en: Opinion is a Latin thinking-verb turned noun, so the hooks follow the act of the mind taking a position rather than any object in the world.
normalIntro.cn: opinion 是拉丁语「思考」动词变来的名词，所以记忆钩子顺着头脑站定位置的动作走，而不是顺着世上的物件走。

normal.en: The Latin verb opinari means to think or suppose, and opinio is simply the noun made from it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为思考、揣度，opinio 就是由它造出的名词。

normal.en: In my opinion is the phrase that shows the word's honesty: the speaker marks the statement as a view, not a fact.
normal.cn: in my opinion 这句搭配正显出这个词的诚实：说话人把话标成看法，而不是事实。

normal.en: A second opinion is a judgement invited from another expert, which is why the word can mean advice as well as belief.
normal.cn: a second opinion 是另请一位专家给出的判断，所以这个词除了信念也能指意见。

normal.en: Opinionated adds a suffix of possession: a person so full of opinions that listening stops.
normal.cn: opinionated 加的是表示「充满」的词尾：一个人满到自己都听不进别人的话。

normal.en: Public opinion is private views counted together, so the word moves from one head to a whole crowd.
normal.cn: public opinion 是把私人看法合起来数，于是这个词从一个脑袋走到一整群人。

abstract.en: A word built on not knowing is the honest companion of every argument, because it leaves room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「尚未确知」之上的词，是一切争论的诚实伙伴，因为它给对方留了位置。

abstract.en: Opinion and fact live beside each other, and much of daily speech is spent sorting which is which.
abstract.cn: 看法与事实并排而立，日常说话有大半时间都用在校准哪句是哪类。

abstract.en: When many opinions agree, they stop sounding like opinions and start sounding like the weather.
abstract.cn: 当许多看法彼此一致，它们就不再像看法，而开始像天气一样被谈论。

examples.en: In my opinion, the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 依我看，这个方案还需要更多时间。

examples.en: Public opinion changed quickly after the report.
examples.cn: 报告公布之后，公众舆论很快转变。

examples.en: The doctor asked her to seek a second opinion.
examples.cn: 医生请她再去求一份专业意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶皮您」——有人偶而皮一下，您还认真听他的意见；记住 opinion 是看法、意见。

root: 来自拉丁语 opinio（看法），再上溯动词 opinari（以为、揣度），经古法语 opinion 进入英语；同族词都围绕「无确证而判断」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a view held without proof; the senses divide by who holds it and how much weight it carries, from one person's belief to expert advice to the public voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是未经确证而持有的看法；义项按持有者与分量分出，从个人信念，到专业意见，再到公众声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded slip of paper opened out, a single sentence in somebody's handwriting still wet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿。

branches.en: two people talking late on a balcony
branches.cn: 两个人在阳台上聊到很晚

branches.en: a patient asking another doctor to look again
branches.cn: 病人请另一位医生再看一次

branches.en: a crowd changing its mind after a report
branches.cn: 一群人读了报告后改变想法

branches.en: a debate that facts alone cannot close
branches.cn: 仅凭事实无法了结的争论

branches.en: the same private view growing into a public force
branches.cn: 同一种私人看法长成公共力量

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of thinking with a noun ending attached; English then adds endings that mark a person too fond of views and a matter open to dispute.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「思考」动词接上名词词尾而成；英语随后又加上词尾，用来指过分爱持看法的人，以及可供争论的事。

latinIntro.en: Latin opinari, opinio and opinabilis are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry behind its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 opinari、opinio、opinabilis 均有记录，因此这一族英语词形背后有可靠的拉丁语世系。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词词尾

definition_zh: 对手；反对者；对立的一方
definition_en: a person or side that competes against another in a contest, argues against a proposal, or stands on the other side of a dispute
core_image: 两张长桌从两边同时被推往中间，桌面在中央顶住，谁也无法再前进一寸
scene: 辩论厅的灯全开着，两张长桌面对面摆好，一边的人翻开稿子，另一边的人已经站了起来。Her main opponent in the debate had prepared for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里的 opponent 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：比赛或辩论中正面对垒的一方）；句意为她在辩论中的主要对手准备了数周。图中可辨识物件：长桌、稿子、站起的人。

pos.zh: 对手；反对者；对立的一方

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 oppositio 而来，词干取自 opponere 的分词，义为「反对；对立面」
由动词 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；相反的」
由 opposition 加 -al 构成，义为「对抗性的；反对派的」

senses.title: A rival in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that is trying to win the same prize or beat the same record as you
senses.definitionCN: 与你争夺同一个奖项、或试图打破同一纪录的人或队伍
senses.example: She beat her opponent in three straight sets.
senses.exampleCN: 她连下三盘击败了对手。
senses.why: Latin opponere meant to set one thing against another, so a contest puts two people on opposite sides of the same board.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opponere 意为把一物置于另一物对面，所以一场比赛就是把两个人放在同一块棋盘的两边。

senses.title: A person who argues against something
senses.definition: a person who speaks or votes against a plan, policy or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、政策或主张发言反对或投反对票的人
senses.example: The proposal had more opponents than supporters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议的反对者比支持者更多。
senses.why: The same verb of setting against works in speech: a view is placed opposite another view, and the person holding it becomes the opponent.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「置于对面」的动词也用于言语：一种主张被摆到另一种主张对面，持这种主张的人就成了反对者。

senses.title: Belonging to the other side
senses.definition: standing on the opposite side in a contest, dispute or armed conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、争端或武装冲突中站在另一边的
senses.example: The opponent army withdrew before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 对方军队在黎明前撤离。
senses.why: Because the word began as a participle meaning the one placed opposite, it could also describe the side itself rather than only a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是分词，意为「被置于对面的那个」，因此它也能形容那一方本身，而不只是某个人。

senses.title: A force or thing working against another
senses.definition: something that pulls, pushes or works in the opposite direction to another thing
senses.definitionCN: 朝相反方向拉扯、推动或运行的事物
senses.example: Each muscle in the arm has an opponent that moves the joint back.
senses.exampleCN: 手臂上每块肌肉都有一块把它反向拉回的对抗肌。
senses.why: The image of two things set against each other extends from people to bodies: whatever pulls one way has a counterpart pulling the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物相互对置的画面从人扩展到身体：凡朝一边拉的，都会有一个朝另一边拉的对应物。

intro.en: Opponent is the Latin participle of a verb meaning to set against, and English took it as a noun for whoever stands opposite; the same verb also gives oppose and opposite.
intro.cn: opponent 是拉丁语中意为「置于对面」的动词的分词形式，英语把它用作名词，指站在对面的那个人；同一动词也给出 oppose 与 opposite。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant toward, against or in the way of, and before p it regularly took the form op-.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 意为朝向、对着、挡在前方，在 p 之前习惯变为 op-。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it is the placing verb behind a whole family of English words.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、摆下，是英语一整族词背后的「放置」动词。

items.en: Ob- plus ponere gave opponere, to set against or place in the way, used of objects, arguments and opponents alike.
items.cn: ob- 与 ponere 合成 opponere，意为置于对面或挡在路前，物件、论点和对手都能用。

items.en: The present participle opponentem named the person doing the setting against, and this form is the direct parent of the English noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 opponentem 指正在「置之于对面」的人，这一形式正是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Modern English uses opponent for rivals, for those who argue against a plan, for the opposing side, and for anything that pulls the other way.
items.cn: 现代英语用 opponent 指竞争者、反对某项计划的人、对方阵营，以及任何向反方向拉扯的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb ponere, which is about placing; the near-meaning group collects other names for the person or side you face.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 ponere（放置）上的词；近义组收其他指「你所面对的人或一方」的名称。

entries.definition: To act or speak against something.
entries.definitionCN: 行动上或言语上反对某事。

entries.definition: The act of resisting, or the side that resists.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗的行为，或进行抵抗的一方。

entries.definition: Placed facing something else, or as different as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 面朝另一物放置的，或差别尽可能大的。

entries.definition: To put forward an idea or question for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 把观点或问题提出来供他人考虑。

entries.definition: A person competing for the same goal as another.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标与他人竞争的人。

entries.definition: A person or group on the other side of a conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 冲突中站在另一边的人或群体。

entries.definition: A person or firm trying to do better than others.
entries.definitionCN: 力图胜过他人的个人或公司。

entries.definition: An enemy in battle or in a long quarrel.
entries.definitionCN: 战斗或长期争斗中的敌人。

normalIntro.en: Opponent is a Latin participle doing noun work, so the hooks keep the picture of something placed directly opposite something else.
normalIntro.cn: opponent 是拉丁语分词在充当名词，所以记忆钩子始终保留「一物被摆在另一物正对面」的画面。

normal.en: Opponent is the participle of opponere, the one set against, so the ending marks a person in the middle of the action.
normal.cn: opponent 是 opponere 的分词，指被置于对面的那个人，词尾标出的正是一个身处动作中的人。

normal.en: The prefix is ob- before p, which is why opponent looks like oppose but not like obvious.
normal.cn: 前缀是 p 前的 ob-，所以 opponent 与 oppose 相像，却与 obvious 不同。

normal.en: Opposition comes from the same verb through its participle stem opposit-, so the pair keeps one root.
normal.cn: opposition 经由分词词干 opposit- 出自同一动词，两者共用一个词根。

normal.en: The hand has an opponens muscle that pulls the thumb across the palm, literally setting it against the fingers.
normal.cn: 手部有一块对掌肌，名字直译就是把拇指移到手指对面，正是「置于对面」的本义。

normal.en: In a debate, an opponent faces you; on the battlefield, the opponent army faces yours, and the word fits both.
normal.cn: 辩论时对手正面朝你；战场上对方军队正对你的军队，这个词两处都合用。

abstract.en: A word for the person opposite reminds us that a contest is always a pair, never one side alone.
abstract.cn: 指「对面那个人」的词提醒我们：一场较量总是成双的，从不只有一边。

abstract.en: Setting something against something else is how arguments begin, and the word does not say who is right.
abstract.cn: 把一物置于另一物对面，正是争论的开始，而这个词并不判定谁对。

abstract.en: Even inside the body, every pull has a counter-pull, and English borrowed the same noun for that quiet balance.
abstract.cn: 即便在身体里，每一次牵拉都有反向牵拉，英语也用同一个名词来指这份沉默的平衡。

examples.en: She beat her opponent in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 她连下三盘击败了对手。

examples.en: The proposal had more opponents than supporters.
examples.cn: 这项提议的反对者比支持者更多。

examples.en: Each muscle has an opponent that pulls the joint back.
examples.cn: 每块肌肉都有一块把关节反向拉回的对抗肌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶碰能」——两人偶一碰上，就得比一比谁能站稳；记住 opponent 是对手。

root: 来自拉丁语 opponere（置于对面）的现在分词 opponentem，由 ob-（朝向、对着，在 p 前变 op-）与 ponere（放置）合成。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing placed against another; from that face-to-face position come the rival, the person who argues back, the opposing side and the counter-pull in a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一物被置于另一物对面；从这个正面对峙的位置分出竞争者、出言反对的人、对方阵营，以及身体里的反向牵拉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two long tables pushed from opposite sides until they meet and neither can move further.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张长桌从两边同时被推往中间，桌面在中央顶住，谁也无法再前进一寸。

branches.en: two players waiting on opposite sides of a net
branches.cn: 球网两边各自等着的两个球员

branches.en: a hall where a proposal is spoken against
branches.cn: 提案被人出言反对的大厅

branches.en: a column advancing toward another column
branches.cn: 朝另一支队伍推进的队伍

branches.en: a muscle pulling a joint back the other way
branches.cn: 把关节反向拉回的肌肉

branches.en: the same word for the body opposite and the voice against
branches.cn: 同一个词，兼指对面的身体与反对的声音

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of opposition plus the verb for placing, worn into a participle; English adds noun and adjectival endings from there.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「对着」的拉丁前缀与「放置」动词合成、再磨成分词；英语由此再接名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, opponere and oppositio are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry and a clear image of placing one thing against another.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere、opponere、oppositio 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，也有清晰的「把一物置于另一物对面」的画面。

definition_zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会
definition_en: a chance to do something, a favourable moment or set of circumstances, or an opening for work and advancement
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门忽然被推开，门外透进一束亮光，正落在站着的人脚前
scene: 招聘会的走廊里挤满人，一个年轻人停在展位前，把手里那份改过三遍的简历递了出去。She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
sceneCN: 这里的 opportunity 是「机会」（第 1 个义项：可以做某事的时机）；句意为她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。图中可辨识物件：展位、简历、走廊人群。

pos.zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 opportunus 而来，义为「恰好的；及时的」
由 opportune 加 -ism 构成，义为「机会主义；投机」
由 opportunist 加 -ic 构成，义为「投机取巧的；趁机的」

senses.title: A chance to do something
senses.definition: a situation in which it is possible for someone to do something they want or need to do
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以去做自己想做的事或必须做的事的境况
senses.example: She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。
senses.why: The word grew from a picture of a ship reaching a safe harbour, so a chance is imagined as a door that happens to be open just as you arrive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一个船靠上安全港湾的画面长出来，所以机会被想成一扇恰在你到达时敞开的门。

senses.title: A favourable moment
senses.definition: a short period that is especially suitable for acting, and which may not come again
senses.definitionCN: 特别适合行动的一段短时间，而且可能不会再来
senses.example: The quiet morning was the best opportunity to raise the matter.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的早晨是提这件事的最好时机。
senses.why: If the chance depends on the moment, then it can pass, and the word comes to mean the right hour rather than any possibility at all.
senses.whyCN: 既然机会取决于时刻，它就可能溜走，于是这个词指的是恰当的时刻，而不是任何可能性。

senses.title: Circumstances that favour success
senses.definition: a combination of conditions that makes progress or success more likely for someone
senses.definitionCN: 让某人更可能取得进展或成功的一组条件
senses.example: Growing up near the sea gave him opportunities his cousins never had.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边长大，给了他表兄弟们从未有过的机遇。
senses.why: Harbour and wind are conditions rather than actions, so the word also names the favourable state of things that lets a person move forward.
senses.whyCN: 港湾与风是条件而不是动作，所以这个词也指那种有利的境况，让人能够向前走。

senses.title: An opening for work or advancement
senses.definition: a post, vacancy or route by which someone may find work or move up
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以找到工作或向上发展的职位、空缺或门路
senses.example: The paper lists job opportunities every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸每周日刊登招聘信息。
senses.why: A post that is open is literally a door left ajar, so employment and promotion are described with the same word as any other chance.
senses.whyCN: 一个空缺的职位本就是一扇虚掩的门，因此就业与晋升也用同一个词来描述，和其他机会并无分别。

intro.en: Opportunity comes from a Latin word for a wind that carries a ship toward harbour; the exact formation is generally explained as a phrase meaning toward the port, though some sources call it uncertain.
intro.cn: opportunity 来自拉丁语中表示「把船吹向港湾的风」的词；其构成一般认为出自意为「朝向港口」的说法，也有资料称来源不确定。

items.en: The usual explanation takes the source as ob portum, toward the harbour, the wind that lets a ship come safely in.
items.cn: 通常的解释把来源看作 ob portum，即「朝向港口」，指让船安全入港的那阵风。

items.en: From that phrase came opportunus, meaning favourable, timely or coming at the right moment, said first of winds and then of anything useful.
items.cn: 由这一短语得出 opportunus，意为有利的、适时的、来得正好的，先用于风，后用于任何合宜之物。

items.en: The noun opportunitas named the quality of being timely, and it could also mean a favourable opening or occasion.
items.cn: 名词 opportunitas 指「合宜」这种性质，也可指有利的时机或场合。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opportunite, meaning a good chance or a suitable time, and English borrowed it with that practical sense.
items.cn: 古法语以 opportunite 承袭该名词，意为好机会或合适的时刻，英语借入时也带着这种实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps opportunity for chances, for the right moment, for favourable conditions and for openings in work.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opportunity 兼指机会、恰当时刻、有利条件，以及工作上的空缺。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of timeliness and harbour; the near-meaning group collects other names for a chance that can be used.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「合时、港湾」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示「可以利用的机会」的名称。

entries.definition: Coming at a good moment; well timed.
entries.definitionCN: 来得正好的；适时的。

entries.definition: Taking advantage of chances without regard to principle.
entries.definitionCN: 不顾原则地利用机会的做法。

entries.definition: A person who uses every chance for personal gain.
entries.definitionCN: 利用一切机会谋取私利的人。

entries.definition: A possibility that something may happen or be done.
entries.definitionCN: 某事可能发生或可能做成的可能性。

entries.definition: A gap or vacancy that allows someone to enter or begin.
entries.definitionCN: 让人得以进入或开始的缺口、空缺。

entries.definition: A particular time at which something happens or may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生或可能发生的特定时刻。

entries.definition: A limited period during which action is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以采取行动的一段有限时期。

normalIntro.en: Opportunity began as weather and harbour talk, so its hooks keep a ship, a wind and an open door rather than any abstract idea of luck.
normalIntro.cn: opportunity 起初是谈天气与港湾的话，所以记忆钩子守着一艘船、一阵风和一道敞开的门，而不是抽象的运气。

normal.en: The Latin phrase behind the word means toward the harbour, and opportunus first described a wind that helped a ship in.
normal.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「朝向港口」，opportunus 最初形容把船送进港的风。

normal.en: Opportune is the adjective, and opportunity is that adjective plus -ity, the suffix that turns a quality into a noun.
normal.cn: opportune 是形容词，opportunity 就是它加 -ity，这个后缀把一种性质变成名词。

normal.en: Seize the opportunity and a golden opportunity are fixed pairings: both treat the chance as something that can be grabbed or missed.
normal.cn: seize the opportunity 与 a golden opportunity 都是固定搭配：两者都把机会当成可以抓住或失去的东西。

normal.en: Equal opportunity is a phrase built on the same word, but it speaks of fairness rather than luck.
normal.cn: equal opportunity 也建立在同一个词上，但它讲的是公平，而不是运气。

normal.en: The spelling keeps double p and double t because both came from the Latin forms, so write opportunity with care.
normal.cn: 这个拼写保留双 p 与双 t，因为两者都来自拉丁形式，所以书写时要留意。

abstract.en: A word made from a harbour wind suggests that opportunity is not made but met, and only if you are ready to sail.
abstract.cn: 一个由港湾之风造出的词说明：机会不是被制造的，而是被遇上的，而且只有你准备好起航才算数。

abstract.en: Every chance carries an expiry, which is why the same word can mean a moment and a door.
abstract.cn: 每个机会都带着期限，所以同一个词既能指一段时刻，也能指一道门。

abstract.en: What looks like luck in one life is often a favourable set of conditions that someone else never had.
abstract.cn: 在一个人身上看似运气的东西，往往是一组别人从未拥有的有利条件。

examples.en: She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
examples.cn: 她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。

examples.en: The morning was the best opportunity to raise the matter.
examples.cn: 早晨是提这件事的最好时机。

examples.en: The paper lists job opportunities every Sunday.
examples.cn: 这份报纸每周日刊登招聘信息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶破丢你提」——好机会偶一出现，可别把它丢掉；记住 opportunity 是机会。

root: 来自拉丁语 opportunus（适时的、有利的），一般认为出自 ob portum（朝向港口）这一说法；其名词 opportunitas 经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a favourable opening; the senses divide by how it is used, as a plain chance, a fleeting moment, a set of good conditions, or a post that can be taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一道有利的开口；义项按用法分出：普通机会、稍纵即逝的时刻、有利的境况，以及可以取得的职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door suddenly pushed open, a beam of light falling at the feet of the person standing there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇原本关着的门忽然被推开，门外透进一束亮光，正落在站着的人脚前。

branches.en: a hand reaching out with a folded CV
branches.cn: 一只手递出折好的简历

branches.en: early light before the day fills with noise
branches.cn: 白昼尚未喧闹时的晨光

branches.en: a childhood spent beside the water
branches.cn: 在水边度过的童年

branches.en: a page of job notices in a Sunday paper
branches.cn: 周日报纸上的一版招聘启事

branches.en: the same chance seen as a door and as an hour
branches.cn: 同一个机会，既看成门，也看成时辰

intro.en: The word is a Latin phrase about harbour and wind turned into an adjective, then into a noun, and English adds the endings that name a moment and a person who uses it.
intro.cn: 这个词由一句关于港湾与风的拉丁短语变成形容词、再变成名词，英语又加上词尾，用来指一个时刻和一个善用机会的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin opportunus, opportunitas and portus are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry, even though the phrase behind it is explained in more than one way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 opportunus、opportunitas、portus 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，尽管其背后的短语有不止一种解释。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 反对；抗争；与……对垒；与……相对
definition_en: to speak or act against something in order to stop it, to resist a force, to compete against someone, or to stand in contrast to something
core_image: 一块木板被人从两边同时顶住，中间微微弯起，谁也没有松手
scene: 村口的广场上聚起人群，一块画着道路规划的木板靠在树上，几个人指着板子大声争论。Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
sceneCN: 这里的 opposed 是「反对」（第 1 个义项：不同意并试图阻止某项计划）；句意为多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。图中可辨识物件：木板、树、围拢的人群。

pos.zh: 反对；抗争；与……对垒；与……相对

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 oppositio 而来，词干取自 opponere 的分词，义为「反对；对立」
由拉丁语 oppositus 而来，义为「相反的；对面的」
由 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；反对的」
由拉丁语 opponere 的现在分词而来，义为「对手；反对者」

senses.title: To disagree with and try to stop something
senses.definition: to say or do something against a plan, idea or action in order to prevent it
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、主张或行动表示异议并设法阻止
senses.example: Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
senses.exampleCN: 多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。
senses.why: Latin opponere meant to place something in the way, so opposing a plan is imagined as putting an obstacle in its path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opponere 意为把东西挡在路上，所以反对一项计划，被想成在它的路上放一个障碍。

senses.title: To resist a powerful force or authority
senses.definition: to struggle against a government, army or other power that is stronger than you
senses.definitionCN: 与比自己更强大的政府、军队或其他力量相抗争
senses.example: The villagers opposed the dam for years without success.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们为反对这座水坝抗争多年，却没有成功。
senses.why: When the thing in the way is a whole power rather than a plan, the same verb turns from objecting into resisting.
senses.whyCN: 当挡在前面的是一整个强权而不是一份计划时，同一个动词就从「提出异议」转为「抵抗」。

senses.title: To compete against someone
senses.definition: to take part in a contest, election or game against another person or team
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或对局中与另一人或另一队相争
senses.example: The two teams will oppose each other in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 两支队伍将在决赛中互相对垒。
senses.why: A contest also places two sides opposite each other, so the verb that means setting against serves games and elections as well.
senses.whyCN: 比赛同样把两边摆到彼此对面，于是这个意为「置于对面」的动词也能用于球赛和选举。

senses.title: To stand in contrast to something
senses.definition: to be set on the other side of a comparison, as in the phrase as opposed to
senses.definitionCN: 在比较中被放在另一边，如固定说法 as opposed to 所示
senses.example: The job needs patience as opposed to speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作要的是耐心，而不是速度。
senses.why: The verb began as a picture of two things facing each other, and comparison keeps that picture: one thing is placed against another to show the difference.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词起初是一幅两物正面对望的画面，比较正保留了这幅画：把一物置于另一物对面，以显出差别。

intro.en: Oppose came into English from Old French, which had reshaped the Latin verb opponere, to set against; the English family still keeps that image of an obstacle placed in the way.
intro.cn: oppose 由古法语进入英语，而古法语改造了拉丁语动词 opponere（置于对面）；这一族英语词仍保留「把障碍挡在路上」的画面。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant toward, against or in front of, and before p it appears as op-, as in opponere and oppose.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 意为朝向、对着、在……之前，在 p 前写作 op-，如 opponere 与 oppose。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it stands behind a large family of English verbs about positioning.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、摆下，是英语一大族表示「安放位置」的动词背后的词。

items.en: Ob- plus ponere gave opponere, to set against or place in the way, used of shields, arguments and rivals.
items.cn: ob- 与 ponere 合成 opponere，意为置于对面或挡在路上，盾牌、论点和对手都能用。

items.en: Old French remade the verb as opposer, meaning to set against or to object, and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词改造成 opposer，意为置于对面或提出异议，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses oppose for objecting, for resisting power, for competing and for the contrast in as opposed to.
items.cn: 现代英语用 oppose 表示提出异议、抵抗强权、参与竞争，以及 as opposed to 中的对比。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb for placing; the near-meaning group collects verbs for standing against something or someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「放置」动词上的词；近义组收表示「对某事或某人站到对面」的动词。

entries.definition: The person or side that stands against you.
entries.definitionCN: 站在你对面的那个人或一方。

entries.definition: The act of resisting, or the group that resists.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗的行为，或进行抵抗的群体。

entries.definition: Facing the other way, or as different as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向另一边的，或差别尽可能大的。

entries.definition: Able to be placed against another finger, as a thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 能与别的手指对置的，如拇指。

entries.definition: To try to stop something that is pushing against you.
entries.definitionCN: 设法挡住正向你压来的东西。

entries.definition: To say that one disagrees with a plan or statement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示对某项计划或说法不赞同。

entries.definition: To refuse openly to obey a person or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从某人或某条规矩。

entries.definition: To argue that something is wrong or not true.
entries.definitionCN: 争论某事有误或不实。

normalIntro.en: Oppose keeps the Latin verb for placing under a prefix of opposition, so the hooks picture a barrier set down in front of something moving.
normalIntro.cn: oppose 在表示「对着」的前缀下保留了拉丁语「放置」动词，所以记忆钩子想的是在某物前进的路上放下一道障碍。

normal.en: The prefix is op-, the form ob- takes before p, so oppose and opponent share a beginning for the same reason.
normal.cn: 前缀是 op-，也就是 ob- 在 p 前的形式，所以 oppose 与 opponent 的开头出于同一个道理。

normal.en: Old French opposer stands between the Latin verb and the English word, which is why the spelling ends in -ose rather than -ere.
normal.cn: 古法语 opposer 夹在拉丁动词与英语词之间，所以拼写以 -ose 而非 -ere 收尾。

normal.en: Be opposed to is the passive shape of the same verb: to be placed opposite something is to hold a view against it.
normal.cn: be opposed to 是同一动词的被动形式：被摆到某物对面，也就是对它持反对看法。

normal.en: As opposed to sets two things side by side so that the difference shows, and it keeps the original picture of facing.
normal.cn: as opposed to 把两样东西并排摆出，让差别显形，保留的正是「面对面」的原画面。

normal.en: Opposed takes a single s while the base oppose has a double p, so check both letters when writing the forms.
normal.cn: opposed 只有一个 s，而原形 oppose 是双 p，书写这些形式时两组字母都要留意。

abstract.en: To oppose is to put your weight on one side of a board and hope the other side gives way first.
abstract.cn: 反对就是把重量压到木板的一边，指望另一边先让步。

abstract.en: The same verb covers a spoken objection and a long resistance, because both begin by standing in the way.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既指一句口头异议，也指长年的抵抗，因为两者都从「挡在路上」开始。

abstract.en: A comparison is a quiet form of opposition: nothing is fought, but two things are still placed face to face.
abstract.cn: 比较是一种安静的对抗：没有争战，但两样东西仍被摆成面对面。

examples.en: Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
examples.cn: 多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。

examples.en: She is strongly opposed to any change in the schedule.
examples.cn: 她强烈反对对日程作任何改动。

examples.en: The job needs patience as opposed to speed.
examples.cn: 这份工作要的是耐心，而不是速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶剖事」——偶一剖开事情的原委，就有人站出来反对；记住 oppose 是反对、抗争。

root: 来自古法语 opposer，再上溯拉丁语 opponere（置于对面），由 ob-（对着、在前，在 p 前变 op-）与 ponere（放置）合成。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a barrier placed in the way; the senses divide by what stands on the other side, a plan, a power, a rival team, or a point of comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是挡在路上的一道障碍；义项按对面是什么分出：一份计划、一股强权、一支对手队伍，或一个比较项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board held from both sides at once, bending slightly in the middle, with neither hand letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板被人从两边同时顶住，中间微微弯起，谁也没有松手。

branches.en: neighbours pointing at a road plan on a board
branches.cn: 邻居们指着木板上的道路方案

branches.en: villagers standing before a rising dam
branches.cn: 村民站在渐渐升高的大坝前

branches.en: two teams walking onto the same field
branches.cn: 两支队伍走进同一片场地

branches.en: patience set beside speed in one sentence
branches.cn: 同一句话里并排放着的耐心与速度

branches.en: the same verb for a loud objection and a quiet contrast
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既指高声异议，也指无声对照

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of a prefix meaning against and the verb for placing, reshaped by French and fitted with English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中「对着」前缀与「放置」动词的复合词，经法语改造，再接上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, opponere and oppositus are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry and a clear picture of something set in the way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere、opponere、oppositus 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，也有清晰的「某物被挡在路上」的画面。

items.meaning: able to be placed against another part

definition_zh: 对面的；相反的；对立的；对立面；对手；在…对面
definition_en: placed on the other side of something and facing it, or completely different and contrary in nature; as a noun, the person, thing or word that stands against another; as a preposition, across from
core_image: 一条窄街两侧正对着的两扇窗，一边亮着灯，一边漆黑
scene: 雨后的窄街两侧，两扇窗正对着，一边亮着暖黄的灯，一边漆黑。The two houses stand opposite each other across the narrow street.
sceneCN: 这里 opposite 是「在…对面」（第 3 个义项：介词，处在另一侧）；句意为两栋房子隔着窄街相对而立，画面是雨后小街与两扇正对的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 opponere 经法语进入英语，义为「反对；对抗」
由 oppose 加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「反对；对立；反对党」
由拉丁语 opponere 的现在分词词干加 -ent 构成，义为「对手；反对者」
由 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；反对的」

senses.title: Facing across from another
senses.definition: placed on the other side of something, so that the two sides look towards each other
senses.definitionCN: 处在某物的另一侧，两者正面相对
senses.example: The shop is on the opposite side of the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店在路的对面。
senses.why: Latin ob- means against or facing, and ponere means to place, so oppositus is literally placed facing something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ob- 表示「对着、面向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 oppositus 字面就是「被放成面对面」；这个义项说的正是空间上正对的那一侧。

senses.title: Completely different or contrary
senses.definition: very different from something else, especially so that the two cannot both be true or both be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为不同，尤指两者不能同时成立或同时选择
senses.example: Her account of the evening was the opposite of his.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那晚的说法和他的完全相反。
senses.why: Two things placed face to face look in contrary directions, so the picture of facing turns into the idea of contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 两个东西一旦面对面摆好，朝向就是相反的；「相对而立」的画面于是转成「说法、性质彼此相反」的抽象意义，重点从位置移到矛盾。

senses.title: Across from; facing
senses.definition: in a position on the other side of something and directly facing it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一侧，并正对着它
senses.example: She sat opposite me at the small table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在小桌子对面，正对着我。
senses.why: The preposition freezes the spatial picture: two things placed against each other with a gap between them, and the word only names the position.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法把这个空间画面固定下来：两样东西隔着一段距离互相对着；此时词只负责指出位置，不再涉及抽象的对立。

senses.title: The person or thing set against another
senses.definition: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another, or a word that expresses the contrary
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物差异最大的一方，也指表示相反意思的词
senses.example: In the debate, the two speakers were exact opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中，两位发言人的立场截然相反。
senses.why: Once the adjective names the far side, it can stand alone as a noun for whatever occupies that far side.
senses.whyCN: 既然形容词能指「远的那一侧」，它就可以单独作名词，指占据那一侧的人、物或词；从描述位置转为指称实体。

intro.en: Opposite comes from Latin opponere, to place against, and its history is first physical: things put face to face before ideas could be in conflict.
intro.cn: opposite 出自拉丁语 opponere（放在对面），它的历史先是物理的：先有面对面摆放的东西，才有互相冲突的观念。

items.en: Ob- meant against or towards and ponere meant to place, so opponere was to set one thing in front of another.
items.cn: ob- 表示「对着、朝向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 opponere 就是把一样东西摆到另一样的前面。

items.en: The past participle oppositus described something placed facing another thing, and it kept both the position and the contrast.
items.cn: 过去分词 oppositus 形容被摆成面对另一物的事物，既保留位置，也带出对比。

items.en: Old French took the Latin participle as opposite, meaning placed on the other side, and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁分词写作 opposite，意为「位于另一侧的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English used opposite as an adjective for facing things and as a noun for the side that faces us.
items.cn: 中古英语里 opposite 既作形容词指「相对而立的」，也作名词指「正对着我们的那一方」。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use from the eighteenth century and extends the adjective from space to ideas that contradict each other.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪补上介词用法，并把形容词从空间上的相对扩展到互相矛盾的观点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin verb for placing against; the near-meaning group gathers words for facing positions and contrary senses.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「放在对面」这一动词上的词；近义组收表示面对的位置与相反意义的词。

entries.definition: To act against something or to say that it is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 反对；对抗。

entries.definition: The act of resisting, or the group that resists.
entries.definitionCN: 反对的行为，也指反对的一方。

entries.definition: A person who competes against or argues against another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一人竞争或争论的对手。

entries.definition: Suitable and well placed in relation to the matter at hand; the spelling resembles opposite but the prefix changes the sense to fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 恰当而切题的；拼写与 opposite 相近，前缀不同，侧重「贴合」。

entries.definition: Opposite in direction or in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 方向或性质相反的。

entries.definition: The exact contrary of what has been stated or done.
entries.definitionCN: 所述或所做之事的正相反一面。

entries.definition: Positioned so as to look towards something.
entries.definitionCN: 摆成朝向某物的位置。

entries.definition: On the other side of something and directly facing it.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物的另一侧并正对着它。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a prefix meaning against and a verb meaning to place, so every hook returns to something set down face to face.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「对着」的前缀与表示「放置」的动词构成，所有记忆钩子都回到「面对面摆下」这个动作。

normal.en: Opposite is ob- plus ponere, against plus to place, so the first picture is two objects set down facing each other.
normal.cn: opposite 是 ob- 加 ponere，也就是「对着」加「放置」，最早的画面是两件东西面对面摆好。

normal.en: Oppose keeps the verb alive: to put oneself against something, which is why opposition grows from the same stem.
normal.cn: oppose 保留了动词义：把自己摆到某事对面，所以 opposition 从同一词干长出来。

normal.en: The adjective can become a noun because the far side can be named without saying what it is far from.
normal.cn: 形容词能变成名词，因为「远的那一侧」可以不给参照物就直接被指出来。

normal.en: Opposite side and opposite direction still measure space, while the opposite of measures ideas.
normal.cn: opposite side 与 opposite direction 仍在量空间，the opposite of 则在量想法。

normal.en: English says opposite the bank without a preposition, because the word already carries the across idea inside it.
normal.cn: 英语说 opposite the bank 时不加介词，因为这个词本身已经含有「横过、对面」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture two windows on a narrow street, each lit from within, each facing the other; that pair is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 想象窄街两侧的两扇窗，各自从里面亮着，各自正对另一边；这一对窗就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: Two arrows painted on a road point in contrary ways, and that is how a position becomes a contradiction.
abstract.cn: 路面上画着的两支箭头指向相反，位置上的相对就是这样变成了意义上的矛盾。

abstract.en: Two people across a small table can disagree without moving, and opposite is the gap that holds them apart.
abstract.cn: 隔着张小桌的两个人可以不动地方就彼此不同意，而 opposite 正是把他们隔开的那段距离。

examples.en: The shop is on the opposite side of the road.
examples.cn: 那家店在路的对面。

examples.en: Her account of the evening was the opposite of his.
examples.cn: 她对那晚的说法和他的完全相反。

examples.en: She sat opposite me at the small table.
examples.cn: 她坐在小桌子对面，正对着我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆坐」——阿婆坐在他对面；opposite 就是对面、相反。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（对着）加 ponere（放置）构成 opponere（放在对面），过去分词 oppositus 经古法语 opposite 进入英语；核心始终是「面对面」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a facing position; from there the word divides into the far side, the contrary meaning, the preposition of place, and the noun for a rival.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「面对面」的位置；由此分出远的那一侧、相反的意思、表位置的介词，以及指对手的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two windows on opposite sides of a narrow street, each facing the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：窄街两侧正对着的两扇窗，各自朝向另一边。

branches.en: two windows facing each other over a wet street
branches.cn: 雨后窄街两侧正对着的两扇窗

branches.en: black and white laid side by side
branches.cn: 黑与白并排摆开

branches.en: two people seated across a small table
branches.cn: 隔着小桌对坐的两个人

branches.en: two teams standing on either side of a line
branches.cn: 站在界线两侧的两支队伍

branches.en: one picture of facing, close up at a table or far across a street
branches.cn: 同一幅面对面的画面，近在桌前或远在街对面

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin prefix for against, a Latin verb for placing, and the participle that froze into an English adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「对着」的拉丁前缀、表示「放置」的拉丁动词，以及凝固成英语形容词的分词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to place against or in front of
action or state, as in opposition

definition_zh: 反对；抵抗；在野阵营；对立立场；对比；天体冲；对手；正式异议
definition_en: the act of resisting or arguing against something, or the side that stands against another
core_image: 两排人隔着一条长桌，一边推、一边挡，桌面中线谁都不肯越过
scene: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳。The new road plan ran into strong opposition from residents.
sceneCN: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳；句中的这个词指「来自某群人的抵抗」（第 1 个义项：对某项计划或政策表示反对并设法阻止）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、两排座椅、摊开的提案、举起的手、麦克风；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 反对；抵抗；对立的一方（不可数或可数）

derivatives.zh: 反对；抵抗
相反的；在……对面
对手；反对者
对立的；反对的

senses.title: Resistance to a plan
senses.definition: active disagreement with a proposal, shown by argument, voting or protest
senses.definitionCN: 对某项提议的积极不同意，通过争辩、投票或抗议表现出来
senses.example: Plans for the tower met fierce opposition at the first hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 建塔方案在第一次听证会上遭到激烈反对。
senses.why: The word is built from 'place against': something is set face to face with a plan and pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「放到对面」构成：某样东西被摆到计划对面，然后往回推。

senses.title: The side out of office
senses.definition: the parties or politicians who do not hold government and argue against those who do
senses.definitionCN: 不掌握政府、专门与掌权者争辩的政党或政治人物
senses.example: The opposition voted against the budget in every committee.
senses.exampleCN: 在野阵营在每个委员会都投票反对这份预算。
senses.why: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is literally placed opposite the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 议会席位两两相对，于是没有权力的那一边字面上就被安置在部长们的对面。

senses.title: An opposing stance in debate
senses.definition: the position of the speaker or team that argues against the motion
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中主张反对该项动议的一方所持的立场
senses.example: The debate split into support and opposition before the first recess.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论在第一次休息前就分成了支持与反对两方。
senses.why: A debate is a physical arrangement of voices: one side proposes, the other side is placed against it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论就是声音的排布：一边提出，另一边被安置在它的对面。

senses.title: Contrast or difference
senses.definition: a sharp difference between two things that are set side by side for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两样东西并置比较时显现的鲜明差异
senses.example: The opposition between the two theories is sharper than it looks.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种理论之间的对立比表面上更尖锐。
senses.why: Two things placed opposite each other define their difference by their facing positions.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西相对摆放，正是靠面对面的位置显出彼此的差异。

senses.title: Astronomical opposition
senses.titleCN: 天体冲（行星与太阳相对）
senses.definition: the position in which a planet is on the opposite side of Earth from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 某颗行星位于地球与太阳相对一侧的位置
senses.example: Mars reaches opposition roughly every two years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星大约每两年到达一次冲的位置。
senses.why: In the sky the same geometry works: two bodies sit on opposite sides of the observer and face each other.
senses.whyCN: 天空里也是同一套几何：两个天体位于观测者的两侧，彼此相对。

senses.title: The opposing team
senses.definition: the team or player that one is competing against in a match
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中与之竞争的那支队伍或那名选手
senses.example: The home side beat the opposition by three goals.
senses.exampleCN: 主队以三球击败对手。
senses.why: A match places two teams on opposite halves of the field, and the other half is simply the opposition.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛把两支队伍放在球场的两个半场，另一半就是「对面」。

senses.title: Structural opposition
senses.definition: a relation between two elements that are defined by being different from each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个要素因彼此不同而互相界定所形成的关系
senses.example: The linguist studied the opposition between voiced and voiceless sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家研究浊音与清音之间的对立。
senses.why: In a system, meaning can come from position: each item is what the item opposite it is not.
senses.whyCN: 在一个系统里，意义可以来自位置：每一项就是它对那一项所不是的东西。

senses.title: A formal objection
senses.definition: a written or official statement asking a court or authority to refuse something
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院或主管机关拒绝某项事项的书面或正式陈述
senses.example: The lawyers filed a formal opposition to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们就这项合并提交了正式的反对意见。
senses.why: The physical act of standing against becomes a document that is placed against a request.
senses.whyCN: 「站到对面」这个动作变成了一份文件，被摆到某项申请的对立面。

intro.en: Opposition comes from Latin oppositio, a noun from opponere 'to place against', whose past participle is oppositus. The astronomical and political senses are later extensions of the same geometry. The exact first date in English is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「放到对面」的动词，其过去分词意为「被放到对面的」，相应的名词意为「对立、反对」。天文义与政治义都是同一套位置关系在后来的延伸。它在英语中首见的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to place, to put'. Its participle positus gave position, posit and deposit.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为「放置、安放」。它的分词形式给了「位置」「假定」「存放」等英语词。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus ponere produced opponere 'to place in the way, to set against'. The prefix is assimilated to op- before p.
items.cn: 意为「对着」的前缀加「放置」构成这个动词，表示「挡在路上、放到对面」。前缀在唇音前同化为「欧普」的形式。

items.en: The past participle oppositus meant 'placed against, set opposite'. English opposite comes from the same participle.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为「被放到对面的、相对的」。英语的「相反的、对面的」就出自同一分词。

items.en: The noun oppositio named the act of placing against, and later the state of being opposed.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「放到对面的动作」，后来也指「彼此相对的状态」。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English in the fourteenth century, still with the sense of a position facing another.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带向英语，时间约在十四世纪，当时仍指「面对另一方的位置」。

items.en: The parliamentary sense is generally dated to the eighteenth century and the astronomical one is older in Latin; both are best described as extensions rather than separate words.
items.cn: 议会义一般认为定于十八世纪，天文义在拉丁语中更早；两者都应视为同一词的延伸，而非另立新词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin 'place against' root or a very close spelling; the second group gathers words for resisting, objecting and competing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「放到对面」的词根，或拼写极近；第二组汇集了表示抵抗、反对与竞争的词。

entries.definition: Facing something, or completely different from it. It describes a position or a quality, not an organized campaign of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 指面对某物，或与某物完全不同。它描述位置或性质，不指有组织的抵抗行动。

entries.definition: To argue or vote against something. It is the action; the noun names the action or the side that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指以言辞或投票反对某事。它是动作本身；名词则指这个动作或采取动作的一方。

entries.definition: A person who is against you in a contest or an argument. It names a rival, not the resistance as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指在竞赛或争论中与你相对的人。它指对手，不指整体的抵抗。

entries.definition: Characterized by being against something. It describes a tendency or a style, while the noun names the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有反对特征的。它描述一种倾向或风格，而名词指事物本身。

entries.definition: The act of pushing back, often with force or endurance. It stresses holding one's ground more than stating a case.
entries.definitionCN: 指往回推的行为，常带力量或持久性。它更强调守住阵地，而不是陈述理由。

entries.definition: A reason given for disagreeing, often in a meeting or a court. It is one spoken item, not a whole side.
entries.definitionCN: 指为表示不同意而给出的理由，常出现在会议或法庭上。它是一条说出口的意见，不是一整方。

entries.definition: Disagreement with an authority or an accepted view, often on principle. It can be quiet and individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权威或公认看法的不认同，常出于原则。它可以是安静的、个人的。

entries.definition: A continuing contest between two sides for the same prize. It is about winning, not about blocking a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两方为同一目标持续竞争。它关乎胜负，而不是阻止某项提议。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin picture of placing one thing against another, the derived family, and the fixed phrases of parliaments and matches.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：把一样东西放到另一样对面的拉丁画面、派生词族，以及议会与赛场的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means 'against', the root means 'place': the whole word is a placing against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「对着」，词根意为「放」：整个词就是「放到对面」。

normal.en: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is called the opposition.
normal.cn: 议会席位两两相对，所以没有权力的那一边就被称为反对方。

normal.en: A match puts two teams on opposite halves: the other half is the opposition.
normal.cn: 比赛把两队放在两个半场：另一半就是对手。

normal.en: The family runs oppose, opposite, opponent and oppositional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括反对、相反的、对手与对立的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: meet strong opposition, in opposition to, the official opposition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：遭到强烈反对、与……相对、官方反对党。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs dragged to face each other; whatever sits on one chair is defined by the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子被拖到彼此对面；坐在其中一把上的东西，由另一把来界定。

abstract.en: Opposition is not hatred; it is geometry. The other side is simply the side that faces yours.
abstract.cn: 反对不是仇恨，而是几何：另一边只是与你这一边相对的那一边。

abstract.en: The same geometry explains a debate, a lawsuit, a planet in the sky and a rival team.
abstract.cn: 同一套几何能解释一场辩论、一桩诉讼、天上的一颗行星和一支对手球队。

examples.en: Opposition to the new runway grew after the noise reports were published.
examples.cn: 噪音报告公布后，反对新建跑道的声音变大了。

examples.en: The opposition walked out when the minister refused to answer.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝回答时，反对党阵营退场了。

examples.en: In this system every sound is defined by its opposition to another sound.
examples.cn: 在这个系统里，每个音都由它与另一个音的对立来界定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧波季申」——「欧」的一边「波」到对面，另一边就「季申」申辩，正好是两方对着站

root: 拉丁 opponere「放到对面」（ob-「对着」+ ponere「放」）的过去分词 oppositus，名词 oppositio；同根词包括表示「反对」的动词、表示「对面」的形容词与表示「对手」的名词，以及同出「放置」词根的位置、组合二词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one arrangement: two things are placed face to face, and that facing becomes resistance, a rival side, a contrast, a planet in line, or a filed objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一种摆法出发：两样东西被放到面对面，这种相对就变成抵抗、对立的一方、差异、排成一线的一颗行星，或一份提交的异议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: place one thing against another and let each define the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一样东西放到另一样对面，让彼此互相界定。

branches.en: RESIST AND FILE: one pushes back in the street or the hearing, the other puts the refusal into an official document.
branches.cn: 抵抗与备案：一个在街头或听证会上往回推，另一个把拒绝写成正式文件。

branches.en: RIVAL SIDES: the party out of office and the team on the other half both occupy the facing position.
branches.cn: 互为对手的两方：在野阵营与另一个半场的球队，都占据着面对面的位置。

branches.en: STANCE AND DIFFERENCE: in a debate one takes a side; between two things the side becomes a visible contrast.
branches.cn: 立场与差异：在辩论中选一边；在两样东西之间，这一边就变成可见的对比。

branches.en: CELESTIAL LINE: a planet, the earth and the sun fall into the same facing arrangement.
branches.cn: 天上的连线：行星、地球与太阳排成同一套相对的位置。

branches.en: STRUCTURED PAIR: inside a system, each element is what the element opposite it is not.
branches.cn: 结构中的成对：在一个系统里，每个要素就是与它相对的那个要素所不是的东西。

intro.en: Opposition is built from a Latin prefix meaning 'against', a Latin root meaning 'place', and a Latin noun suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个意为「对着」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「放」的拉丁词根和一个拉丁名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' supplies the root; ob- 'against' supplies direction; -io, -ionem turns the participle into a noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「放」的动词提供词根；意为「对着」的前缀提供方向；名词后缀把分词变成表示动作的名词。

items.structure: ob- (Latin prefix, 'against, in the way of'; assimilated to op- before p)
items.meaningCN: 对着；迎面，语义偏移为「反对」
items.example: The prefix puts the action in someone's way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作挡在某人路上。

items.example: The root appears in compose and position.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在「组成」与「位置」里。

items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面，语义偏移为「反对、抵抗」
items.exampleCN: 几名成员反对这项动议。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的，语义偏移为「相反的、对面的」
items.example: The bank is opposite the station.

items.meaning: the act or state of being against
items.meaningCN: 处于对面的动作或状态，语义偏移为「反对、反对派」
items.example: The plan met opposition at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划立刻遭到反对。

items.structure: op- + ponent (Latin ponens, present participle of ponere)
items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面的人，语义偏移为「对手、反对者」
items.example: Her opponent withdrew before the final.
items.exampleCN: 她的对手在决赛前退出了。

items.meaningCN: 具有反对性质的，语义偏移为「对立的」
items.example: The party adopted an oppositional tone.

items.meaningCN: 放到一起，语义偏移为「组成、创作」

definition_zh: 光学的；与光有关的；视觉的；眼睛的；光学仪器（复数名词）
definition_en: relating to light, to sight, or to devices that use lenses, mirrors or fibres
core_image: 玻璃丝里跑着一串光脉冲，细丝末端亮起一个小点
scene: 玻璃丝里跑着一个个光脉冲，信号沿细丝传到远处的接收端。The optical fibre carries the signal as pulses of light along a glass thread.
sceneCN: 这里 optical 指「与光或光学有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及光的产生、传播或控制的）；句意为光纤把信号以光脉冲形式沿玻璃丝传送。可辨识物件：玻璃细丝、光脉冲、接收端、连接头；对应第 1 个义项。

（常用复数）光学仪器；光学部件

senses.title: Relating to light
senses.definition: concerned with light itself, its production, transmission or detection
senses.definitionCN: 涉及光本身，即其产生、传播或探测
senses.example: The optical fibre carries the signal as pulses of light along a glass thread.
senses.exampleCN: 光纤把信号以光脉冲形式沿玻璃丝传送。
senses.why: Greek optikos meant of sight, from optos, seen; the adjective moved from the eye to the light the eye uses.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 optikos 意为「视觉的」，出自 optos「被看见的」；这个形容词从眼睛移到了眼睛所用的光。

senses.title: An optical instrument
senses.titleCN: 使用透镜或反射镜的光学仪器
senses.definition: describing a device that uses lenses, mirrors or prisms to form an image or direct light
senses.definitionCN: 描述用透镜、反射镜或棱镜成像或导光的装置
senses.example: The laboratory keeps its optical instruments in a dust-free cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把光学仪器放在无尘柜里。
senses.why: the adjective names the working principle rather than the purpose, so a microscope and a camera share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是工作原理而非用途，因此显微镜与相机共用它。

senses.title: An optical illusion
senses.titleCN: 视错觉：眼睛被图案骗过
senses.definition: a false perception produced when the visual system interprets a pattern in the wrong way
senses.definitionCN: 视觉系统对图案作出错误解释时产生的错误感知
senses.example: The optical illusion made the straight lines appear to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个视错觉让直线看起来弯了。
senses.why: the error lies in sight rather than in light, which is why the word keeps its link to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 错误出在视觉而非光线，因此这个词仍与眼睛相连。

senses.title: An optical fibre
senses.titleCN: 光纤：把光约束在细丝中传输
senses.definition: a thin thread of glass that guides light by repeated internal reflection, used to carry signals
senses.definitionCN: 靠反复全反射把光约束其中的细玻璃丝，用于传输信号
senses.example: Optical fibre replaced copper in the new trunk line.
senses.exampleCN: 新干线路上，光纤取代了铜线。
senses.why: the fibre works by optics alone, so the adjective distinguishes it from the electrical cable it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 这种纤维只靠光学工作，因此用该形容词与它取代的电线区分开来。

senses.title: The optical axis
senses.titleCN: 光轴：光学系统的对称中心线
senses.definition: the line through the centre of a lens or mirror system about which the optical elements are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 穿过透镜或反射镜系统中心、各光学元件据以排列的那条线
senses.example: The lens was mounted slightly off the optical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这片透镜安装得略微偏离光轴。
senses.why: a system needs a reference line, and the adjective marks that the line belongs to light rather than to mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 系统需要一条参考线，这个形容词标出这条线属于光而非机械。

senses.title: Optical character recognition
senses.titleCN: 光学字符识别：让机器读印刷文字
senses.definition: the automatic conversion of a picture of printed text into machine-readable characters
senses.definitionCN: 把印刷文字的图像自动转成机器可读字符
senses.example: Optical character recognition turned the scanned page into searchable text.
senses.exampleCN: 光学字符识别把扫描页变成了可检索的文本。
senses.why: the machine looks at the page with light and lenses, so computing borrowed the adjective for the seeing part.
senses.whyCN: 机器用光与镜头看这一页，因此计算机领域借这个形容词指「看」的那一环。

senses.title: Optical astronomy
senses.titleCN: 光学天文学：用可见光观测
senses.definition: the branch of astronomy that observes visible light rather than radio, infrared or other bands
senses.definitionCN: 观测可见光而非射电、红外等波段的天文学分支
senses.example: Optical astronomy still supplies the sharpest pictures of planets.
senses.exampleCN: 光学天文学仍能提供最清晰的行星图像。
senses.why: as other bands opened up, the old visible-light work needed a label, and optical became it.
senses.whyCN: 当别的波段被打开后，旧的可见光工作需要一个标签，optical 便承担了这个角色。

senses.title: Abstract: visual rather than conceptual
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：视觉层面的，而非概念层面的
senses.definition: concerned with how something looks to the eye rather than with what it means
senses.definitionCN: 关注某物在眼睛看来是什么样，而非它意味着什么
senses.example: The disagreement was optical rather than substantive, a matter of layout.
senses.exampleCN: 这一分歧是视觉层面的而非实质性的，只是版式问题。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the channel: something is judged by appearance, not by content.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留通道：判断依据是外观，而非内容。

intro.en: Optical comes through Latin opticus from Greek optikos, of sight, built on optos, seen, from the verb for seeing. The word entered English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: optical 经拉丁 opticus 来自希腊 optikos「视觉的」，其词为 optos「被看见的」，出自「看见」这一动词。这个词在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Ops meant the eye or the face, and the related verb meant to see; the family also gives optos, seen.
items.cn: ops 指眼睛或脸，相关动词意为「看见」；这一族还给出 optos「被看见的」。

items.en: Optikos meant of sight or of the science of seeing, and it named the study of light and vision.
items.cn: optikos 意为「视觉的、看之学的」，并用来说明研究光与视觉的学问。

items.en: Latin took the adjective as opticus; English optical follows the Latin stem with the suffix -al.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 opticus；英语 optical 沿用拉丁词干并加后缀 -al。

items.en: English optical appears in the sixteenth century, first in treatises on lenses and the eye.
items.cn: 英语 optical 出现于十六世纪，最初见于论透镜与眼睛的著作。

items.en: Optical fibre, optical character recognition and optical astronomy are all twentieth-century compounds built on the adjective.
items.cn: 光纤、光学字符识别与光学天文学都是 20 世纪以该形容词构成的复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the further origin of Greek ops is unsettled, and the link sometimes drawn to a Indo-European seeing root is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：希腊 ops 的更早来源没有定论，有人把它与某个印欧「看见」词根相连，那属重构，而非已证实的环节。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like optical but come from different roots or different word classes; group two holds the adjectives that also describe sight and light.
note.cn: 第一组是与 optical 形近、却来自不同词根或不同词类的词；第二组是同样描述视觉与光的形容词。

entries.definition: The science of light, a plural-looking singular noun; it is the discipline, not a property of an object.
entries.definitionCN: 研究光的学科，形式是复数而作单数用；它是学科，不是物体的属性。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells lenses and spectacles, built with -ian marking a practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或售卖镜片与眼镜的人，后缀 -ian 表示从业者。

entries.definition: From optio, a choice, not from ops, the eye; it means not compulsory and has no optical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 optio「选择」，而非 ops「眼睛」；意为「非必需的」，完全没有光学含义。

entries.definition: The profession of measuring vision and prescribing lenses, from optos plus metron, measure.
entries.definitionCN: 测量视力并验配镜片的行业，由 optos 加 metron「测量」构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the act of seeing or to visual perception, as in visual memory.
entries.definitionCN: 与看这一行为或视觉感知有关，如视觉记忆。

entries.definition: Relating to the eye as an organ, as in ocular muscles; it is anatomical rather than physical.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为器官的眼睛有关，如眼肌；属解剖用语而非物理用语。

entries.definition: Relating to light as a stimulus to living things, as in the photic zone of the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 与光作为生物刺激有关，如海洋透光层。

entries.definition: A plain descriptive phrase for equipment built around lenses; it lacks the scientific scope of optical.
entries.definitionCN: 对围绕透镜构造的设备的朴素描述，缺少 optical 的科学涵盖面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real word family and the real twentieth-century compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的词族与真实的 20 世纪复合词。

normal.en: Greek optos means seen, so optical is about what light makes visible.
normal.cn: 希腊 optos 意为「被看见的」，因此 optical 讲的是光使什么可见。

normal.en: Optics is the field, an optician is the person, and optically is the adverb.
normal.cn: optics 是学科，optician 是从业者，optically 是副词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: optical fibre, optical illusion, optical axis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：光纤、视错觉、光轴。

normal.en: Optical astronomy means visible-light astronomy, as opposed to radio astronomy.
normal.cn: 「光学天文学」指依靠可见光的观测分支，与射电天文学相对。

normal.en: Optional looks similar but comes from choice, not from the eye.
normal.cn: optional 形近，却出自「选择」而非「眼睛」。

abstract.en: Picture a thread of glass so clear that only the light inside it shows the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一根玻璃丝清透到只有里面的光能指路。

abstract.en: Picture two parallel lines that insist on looking bent.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线偏要看起来是弯的。

abstract.en: Picture a page that a machine reads with a lamp instead of a mind.
abstract.cn: 想象机器用一盏灯而不是用头脑去读的一页纸。

examples.en: The telescope is the oldest optical instrument still in daily use.
examples.cn: 望远镜是仍被日常使用的最古老光学仪器。

examples.en: Optical fibres carry most of the world long-distance data traffic.
examples.cn: 光纤承载了世界上大部分长途数据流量。

examples.en: The museum uses optical character recognition to index its labels.
examples.cn: 博物馆用光学字符识别为标签建索引。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「opt（看）+ ical」——与看、与光有关的 → 光学的；用镜片和光工作的 → 光学仪器

root: 希腊 ops「眼睛、脸」→ optos「被看见的」→ optikos「视觉的」，经拉丁 opticus 进入英语并加 -al；ops 的更深来源不确定。英语 optical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with light itself, then pass through instruments, illusions, fibres, axes, machine reading and astronomy, and end as a figure for appearance over substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从光本身开始，随后经过仪器、错觉、光纤、光轴、机器识读与天文，最后成为「外观压过实质」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass thread guiding pulses of light to a small bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根玻璃丝把光脉冲引到一个小小的亮点。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL CORE: light produced, transmitted or detected is the trunk of every other sense.
branches.cn: 物理核心：光的产生、传播或探测，是其余义项的树干。

branches.en: HARDWARE: instruments and axes are arranged around the behaviour of light.
branches.cn: 硬件：仪器与光轴都围绕光的行为了布置。

branches.en: THE EYE FAILS: an illusion is an error of sight, not of light.
branches.cn: 眼睛出错：错觉是视觉的错误，而非光的错误。

branches.en: APPLICATIONS: fibre, character recognition and optical astronomy each take one technical face of light.
branches.cn: 应用：光纤、字符识别与光学天文，各取光的某一个技术侧面。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: what is judged is how it looks, not what it is.
branches.cn: 外观：被判断的是它看起来怎样，而不是它是什么。

intro.en: Optical is a Greek adjective that reached English through Latin, and its stem also builds the names of the field and the practitioner.
intro.cn: optical 是经拉丁进入英语的希腊形容词，其词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek optikos became Latin opticus; English added -al. The noun optics keeps the Greek plural ending -ics that marks a field.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 optikos 转为拉丁 opticus，英语再加 -al。名词 optics 保留希腊复数后缀 -ics，用来表示学科。

items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式出现在光电子学中。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of the Greek stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把希腊词干变成形容词。

items.meaning: a maker or seller of lenses

items.example: Optometry checks how the eye focuses.
items.exampleCN: 验光学检查眼睛如何聚焦。

items.meaning: a glass thread that guides light
items.example: The optical fibre runs under the street.

items.meaning: a trick played on the eye
items.example: The optical illusion bent the straight lines.
items.exampleCN: 这个视错觉把直线弄弯了。
