definition_zh: 乐观的；乐观主义的；抱乐观看法的
definition_en: expecting good things to happen or believing that a situation will turn out well, especially when the signs are not encouraging
core_image: 半杯水前，一个人盯着杯里剩下的那一半，嘴角微微上扬
scene: 桌上只剩半杯水，屋里的人却说明天还会有人送水来，语气平稳。She stayed optimistic even after the second rejection letter arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 optimistic 是「乐观的」（第 1 个义项：对结果抱有好转的期待）；句意为第二封拒信到了，她仍然保持乐观，画面是桌上半杯水与平稳的语气。

pos.zh: 乐观的；乐观主义的；抱乐观看法的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 optimum（最好的事物）经法语 optimisme 进入英语，义为「乐观主义」
由 optimism 加表示「持某种看法的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「乐观的人」
由 optimistic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「乐观地」
由 over- 与 optimistic 复合而成，义为「过于乐观的」

senses.title: Expecting a good outcome
senses.definition: believing that something good will happen or that a situation will end well
senses.definitionCN: 相信会有好事发生，或相信局面最终会好转
senses.example: She is optimistic about her chances of getting the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己拿到那份工作抱乐观态度。
senses.why: Latin optimum named the best possible thing, so the word begins with the best outcome already in view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 optimum 指「可能最好的事物」，所以这个词一开始就把最好的结果放在眼前；期望自然朝好的方向走，这是最直接的一层。

senses.title: Remaining hopeful despite unfavourable signs
senses.titleCN: 即使迹象不利仍怀希望的
senses.definition: keeping a hopeful view even when the evidence so far is discouraging
senses.definitionCN: 即便目前的迹象令人泄气，仍保持有希望的看法
senses.example: He remained optimistic after the first two plans failed.
senses.exampleCN: 头两个方案失败后，他仍然保持乐观。
senses.why: If the best outcome is what the mind fixes on, a setback is read as temporary rather than final.
senses.whyCN: 既然心里认定的是最好的结果，挫折就会被读成暂时的，而不是定局；这个义项强调在不利证据面前仍不改判断。

senses.title: Characteristic of the belief that good prevails
senses.definition: belonging to the outlook that treats the world or human affairs as tending towards good
senses.definitionCN: 属于认为世界或人事总体趋向好的那种看法
senses.example: The report takes an optimistic view of the region's economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对该地区经济持乐观看法。
senses.why: The word also labels a whole outlook, not just a mood, because optimism grew into a name for a way of judging the world.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能标一整套看法，而不只是一时情绪，因为 optimism 已经成了判断世界的一种立场之名；形容词便跟着承担这层立场色彩。

intro.en: Optimistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on optimism, a word formed from Latin optimum, the best possible thing.
intro.cn: optimistic 是十九世纪在 optimism 上造出的形容词，而 optimism 由拉丁语 optimum（可能最好的事物）构成。

items.en: Optimus was the irregular superlative of bonus, good, so it meant the best of all.
items.cn: optimus 是 bonus（好的）的不规则最高级，意为「最好的」。

items.en: Optimum named the greatest good or the best possible state, and it gave the later word its target.
items.cn: optimum 指最大的善或可能达到的最佳状态，为后来的词提供了目标。

items.en: French optimisme was coined in the eighteenth century for the view that this world is the best that could exist.
items.cn: 法语 optimisme 于十八世纪造出，用来指「这个世界已是可能存在的最好世界」的看法。

items.en: English borrowed optimism, added optimist for a person who holds it, and formed optimistic with -ic.
items.cn: 英语借入 optimism，加 -ist 指持此看法的人，再用 -ic 造出 optimistic。

items.en: Modern English uses optimistic for a hopeful expectation in daily life, not only for the philosophical doctrine.
items.cn: 现代英语把 optimistic 用在日常生活里「抱有希望」的期待，不再只指哲学学说。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin best-word and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for hope, confidence and a bright temper.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「最好」这个词及其英语同族；近义组收表示希望、信心与明朗性情的词。

entries.definition: The belief that good things are likely or that the world tends towards good.
entries.definitionCN: 相信好结果可能出现、或世界趋向好的看法。

entries.definition: A person who expects good things to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 期待好事发生的人。

entries.definition: The best or most favourable point or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 最好或最有利的点与状态。

entries.definition: Best possible for a given purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 在特定目的下最好的；最优的。

entries.definition: Feeling that something desired may still happen.
entries.definitionCN: 觉得想要的事仍可能发生。

entries.definition: Thinking in a confident and constructive way.
entries.definitionCN: 以自信、建设性的方式思考。

entries.definition: Sure that something will succeed or be right.
entries.definitionCN: 确信某事会成功或正确。

entries.definition: In good spirits and inclined to see the bright side.
entries.definitionCN: 心情好，倾向于看好的一面。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the Latin word for the best, so its hooks return to the best outcome, the person who expects it and the outlook that names it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「最好」的含义，记忆钩子都回到最好的结果、期待它的人，以及以此为名的看法。

normal.en: Optimum means the best possible thing, so optimistic starts by fixing the eyes on the best outcome.
normal.cn: optimum 意为可能最好的事物，所以 optimistic 一开始就把目光钉在最好的结果上。

normal.en: -ist names the person and -ic names the quality, so optimist and optimistic are two faces of one belief.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-ic 指性质，所以 optimist 与 optimistic 是同一种信念的两张面孔。

normal.en: The opposite is pessimistic, built on pessimus, the worst, and the pair measures one scale from both ends.
normal.cn: 反义词 pessimistic 建在 pessimus（最坏的）上，两个词从两端量同一把尺。

normal.en: Optimistic about is the usual frame, and the preposition points the hope at a particular object.
normal.cn: optimistic about 是常见框架，介词把希望指向某个具体对象。

normal.en: Cautiously optimistic shows the word can be softened, because hope may be held with reservations.
normal.cn: cautiously optimistic 说明这个词可以加软化语，因为希望也可以带着保留。

abstract.en: A glass half full is the oldest picture of this word: the eye chooses which half to count.
abstract.cn: 半杯水是这个词最老的画面：眼睛选择去数哪一半。

abstract.en: A rejection letter that is folded but still answered is optimism turned into an action rather than a mood.
abstract.cn: 一封被折起却仍被回复的拒信，是乐观从情绪变成行动的样子。

abstract.en: A forecast of clearing skies after a grey week shows the word reaching forward to a future it cannot yet see.
abstract.cn: 灰暗一周之后「天气转晴」的预报，显示这个词在伸向它尚未看见的未来。

examples.en: She stayed optimistic even after the second rejection letter arrived.
examples.cn: 第二封拒信到了，她仍然保持乐观。

examples.en: The coach sounded optimistic about the team's chances.
examples.cn: 教练对球队的机会听起来很乐观。

examples.en: He is cautiously optimistic that the repairs will finish this week.
examples.cn: 他谨慎乐观地认为维修本周能完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，盼它美」——optimistic 读来像盼着事情变美；盼好结果，就是乐观。

root: 拉丁语 optimus（最好的，bonus 的最高级）→ optimum（最佳）→ 法语 optimisme → 英语 optimism、optimist，再加 -ic 构成 optimistic。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the best outcome in view; the senses spread from expecting it, to holding on to it under bad signs, to a whole outlook that assumes good prevails.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「眼里最好的结果」；义项从期待它，扩展到在不利迹象下仍守住它，再扩展成假定善会占上风的整套看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person before a half-filled glass, eyes fixed on the part that is still there.
core.cn: 核心意象：半杯水前的人，目光落在仍然存在的那一半。

branches.en: a half-filled glass and a steady gaze
branches.cn: 半杯水与平稳的目光

branches.en: a rejection letter folded but still answered
branches.cn: 被折起却仍被回复的拒信

branches.en: a report predicting a region's recovery
branches.cn: 预测某地区复苏的报告

branches.en: one hopeful reading, once of a glass and once of bad news
branches.cn: 同一种向好解读，一次落在水杯上，一次落在坏消息上

branches.en: a standing view of how the world tends to go
branches.cn: 对世界走向的固定看法

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin adjective for good and its superlative for best, then on the French and English nouns that turned that best into a doctrine.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「好」的形容词及其「最好」的最高级，再依托法语与英语名词，把「最好」变成一种主张。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the view that the world is the best possible
items.meaningCN: 认为世界已达最佳的看法

items.meaning: a hopeful view of the future
a person who expects the best

definition_zh: 选择；选项；选择权；（金融）期权；（计算机）选项
definition_en: one of several things that can be chosen; the freedom or right to choose; a right to buy or sell something at a fixed price
core_image: 几张摊开的牌，你伸手只拿起其中一张
scene: 申请研究生时，她在纸上列出三所学校，比较学费、城市和专业方向。She wrote: Each school is one option, and I can keep all three open until the last week.
sceneCN: 这里 option 是「可供选择的方案」（第 1 个义项：可选的事物之一）；句意：每一所学校都是一个选项，我可以把这三所学校都留到最后一刻再决定。图中可辨识物件：申请表、三所学校名单、铅笔、计算器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 选择；选项；可选择的事物

collocations.zh: 保留选择余地；不急于定死

derivatives.zh: 可选的；非强制的
可选地；非强制地
选择；决定
选择退出；退出机制
选择加入；主动订阅

senses.title: One of the things you can choose
senses.definition: one of two or more things that you can choose to have or do
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可供选择的事物中的一个
senses.example: Studying abroad is one option; staying at home is another.
senses.exampleCN: 出国留学是一种选择，留在国内是另一种选择。
senses.why: The word names the item sitting in front of the chooser. Latin optio meant 'choice' as an act; by 1885 English extended it to 'the thing that may be chosen', so the abstract act became a concrete item on a list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指“选择”这个行为，后来指摆在选择者面前的那一项。拉丁语 optio 是“选择”；英语到 1885 年才把它扩展到“可供选择的事物”，抽象行为于是变成了清单上的具体一项。

senses.title: The freedom or right to choose
senses.definition: the power or liberty of choosing, especially when nothing is forced
senses.definitionCN: 选择的能力或自由，尤指没有被强迫时
senses.example: Employees have the option of working from home two days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以选择每周有两天在家办公。
senses.why: From c. 1600 'action of choosing' came the 1630s sense 'power or liberty of choosing'. The emphasis moves from the chosen item to the chooser's open hand: what matters is that the hand is not forced.
senses.whyCN: 从 1600 年前后的“选择行为”，发展出 1630 年代的“选择权、选择自由”。重点从被选的物件移到了选择者那只未被强迫的手。

senses.title: An extra feature you may add
senses.titleCN: 可选配置：加钱才有的附加功能
senses.definition: a feature or piece of equipment that is available only if the buyer chooses and usually pays for it
senses.definitionCN: 只有买家选择并通常额外付费才提供的功能或设备
senses.example: Air conditioning is an option on this model, not standard equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 空调是这款车型的选装配置，不是标配。
senses.why: Here the choice itself is turned into a product. The buyer's open hand is priced: you may take the extra feature or leave it, and either way the base item still works.
senses.whyCN: 这里被出售的正是“选择”本身。选择者那只张开的手被标上了价格：你可以拿这项附加功能，也可以不拿，而基础产品照样能用。

senses.title: Stock option: a right to buy shares
senses.titleCN: 股票期权：按约定价格买股份的权利
senses.definition: a right given to an employee or investor to buy company shares at a set price within a set period
senses.definitionCN: 给予员工或投资者在约定期限内按约定价格购买公司股份的权利
senses.example: The startup offered her stock options as part of the package.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司把股票期权作为薪酬方案的一部分提供给她。
senses.why: A share option is literally a purchased choice: the holder may buy at the fixed price or walk away. The 1755 commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium' is the direct ancestor of this financial use.
senses.whyCN: 股票期权字面上就是“买来的选择权”：持有人可以按固定价格买入，也可以放弃。1755 年那条“支付权利金换得的特权”的商业义，正是这一金融用法的直系祖先。

senses.title: Option contract: a right with a price
senses.titleCN: 期权合约：有价格的权利
senses.definition: a contract giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a stated price before a deadline
senses.definitionCN: 赋予买方在截止日期前按约定价格买入或卖出资产的权利而非义务的合约
senses.example: The fund bought an option to purchase the land at a fixed price.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金买入了按固定价格购买这块土地的选择权。
senses.why: The legal instrument isolates the core idea of the word: a choice that is bought, bounded by a price and a date. The holder pays for the open hand and may still refuse to close it.
senses.whyCN: 这种法律工具把词的核心抽离出来：一个被买下、受价格和日期约束的选择。持有人为那只张开的手付费，并且仍然可以拒绝合拢。

senses.title: The option play in football
senses.titleCN: 美式橄榄球中的“选择战术”
senses.definition: an American football play in which the ball carrier may either pass or run
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中持球者可选择传球或自己带球推进的战术
senses.example: The quarterback kept the ball on the option play.
senses.exampleCN: 四分卫在这个选择战术中自己带球推进。
senses.why: Recorded by 1953, the play gives the carrier two live choices at the moment of action. The name is not about a product or a contract but about a decision still open while the body is already moving.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法记录于 1953 年：战术让持球者在动作发生的瞬间保有两条真实可走的路线。名字说的不是产品或合约，而是身体已经动起来时仍然敞开的选择。

senses.title: A setting or flag in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的选项或参数开关
senses.definition: a selectable setting, flag, or argument that changes how a program behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变程序行为方式的可选设置、开关或参数
senses.example: Add the -v option to see verbose output.
senses.exampleCN: 加上 -v 选项即可查看详细输出。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the everyday sense: a program offers a menu of behaviours, and the user picks one. The choice is now made by typing a flag rather than by pointing at a card.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了日常义：程序把若干行为列成菜单，用户挑一个。选择方式从“指着卡片”变成了“敲一个参数”。

senses.title: Keeping alternatives available
senses.titleCN: 保留余地：让选择继续敞开
senses.definition: in the phrase keep options open, to avoid committing so that alternatives stay available
senses.definitionCN: 用于 keep options open，表示不做出承诺，以便保留其他可能
senses.example: She kept her options open by applying to several programs.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了好几个项目，以此保留选择余地。
senses.why: This phrase makes the open hand visible. Not choosing yet is itself a choice, because the alternatives remain graspable and no single card has been lifted from the table.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让“张开的手”变得可见。暂不选择本身也是一种选择：其他可能仍然可抓，桌上没有哪张牌被真正拿走。

intro.en: Option comes from Latin through French. The date of the English noun is clear; the origin of the Latin verb optare is not, and standard references mark it as uncertain.
intro.cn: option 经由法语来自拉丁语。英语名词的年代清楚，但拉丁动词 optare 的来源并不清楚，通行资料标注为不确定。

items.en: c. 1600, 'action of choosing'; by the 1630s, 'power or liberty of choosing'. The noun entered English through French option (Old French opcion).
items.cn: 约 1600 年记录为“选择的行为”；到 1630 年代为“选择的能力或自由”。名词经法语 option（古法语 opcion）进入英语。

items.en: From Latin optionem (nominative optio) 'choice, free choice, liberty to choose', a noun from optare 'to desire, pray for, choose'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 optionem（主格 optio）“选择、自由选择、选择的自由”，是由 optare“渴望、祈求、选择”构成的名词。

items.en: De Vaan derives optare from Proto-Italic *opeje- 'to choose, grab', from PIE *hopeie-, and compares Hittite epp-/app- 'to take, grab'. This deeper reconstruction is debated, so the ultimate root is source uncertain.
items.cn: De Vaan 把 optare 追溯到原始意大利语 *opeje-“选择、抓取”，再往上到原始印欧语 *hopeie-，并与赫梯语 epp-/app-“拿、抓”比较。这一更深层重构仍有争议，故最底层词源来源不确定。

items.en: 1755 records the commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium'; 1885 records 'thing that may be chosen'. The word thus moved from act to right to object.
items.cn: 1755 年记录商业义“支付权利金换得的特权”；1885 年记录“可供选择的事物”。词义由此从行为走到权利，再走到物件。

items.en: 1953 records the football option play. The computing sense of a selectable flag is a later 20c. extension of the everyday 'choice' meaning.
items.cn: 1953 年记录橄榄球的 option play（选择战术）。计算机中“可选开关”的义项是 20 世纪后期由日常“选择”义扩展而来。

note.en: The first group separates words that merely look like option; the second compares words that really mean a choice.
note.cn: 第一组只把外形相近的词分开；第二组比较真正表示“选择”的词。

entries.definition: a process or set of actions, especially in surgery or business. It starts with op- but comes from Latin opus 'work', not optare.
entries.definitionCN: 操作；手术；业务。它同样以 op- 开头，但来自拉丁语 opus“工作”，而不是 optare。

entries.definition: a belief or judgment not fully proved. It is linked in dictionaries to opinari 'to think', whose own origin is unknown, and is not a form of option.
entries.definitionCN: 意见；看法。词典把它连到 opinari“认为”，而 opinari 本身来源不明，它不是 option 的变形。

entries.definition: relating to light or the eyes. Its opt- goes back to Greek optos 'seen', a different root from Latin optare.
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；视觉的。它的 opt- 来自希腊语 optos“被看见的”，与拉丁语 optare 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: in grammar, a mood that expresses a wish. It is built directly on Latin optare 'to wish', so it is a true relative of option.
entries.definitionCN: 语法中的祈愿语气。它直接由拉丁语 optare“希望”构成，因此是 option 的真正同族词。

entries.definition: the act of choosing, or the range of things from which one may choose. It is the everyday word; option is more formal and often implies a listed alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 选择的行为，或可供选择的整体范围。它是最日常的词；option 更正式，常指清单上列出的一个备选。

entries.definition: one of two or more possibilities that can replace each other. It stresses replacement; option stresses that the thing is available to pick.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个可相互替代的可能之一。它强调“替换”，option 强调“可供挑选”。

entries.definition: the act of selecting, or the set of things chosen. It often refers to a curated range rather than a single item.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的行为，或被挑出的一组事物。它常指经过整理的一组，而不是单个选项。

entries.definition: a stronger liking for one thing over another. It names the ranking in the chooser's mind, not the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物更强的偏好。它指选择者心里的排序，而不是被选的那个事物。

normalIntro.en: Five sound-and-spelling hooks, then three abstract images for the idea behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住这个词背后的观念。

normal.en: op- sounds like 'open': an option is a door left open until you walk through one.
normal.cn: op- 听起来像 open（打开）：option 就是一扇直到你走进某一间之前都开着的门。

normal.en: -tion marks an action, as in action: choosing is something you do, not a thing that happens to you.
normal.cn: -tion 像 action 里的那个 -tion，标记“动作”：选择是你做的事，不是落到你身上的事。

normal.en: opt out is 'choose out', opt in is 'choose in': the same root with opposite directions.
normal.cn: opt out 是“选出去”（退出），opt in 是“选进来”（加入）：同一个词根，方向相反。

normal.en: Keep options open = keep the cards on the table, not in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep options open＝把牌留在桌上，而不是揣进口袋。

normal.en: optional ends in -al like 'additional': an optional extra is one you may add.
normal.cn: optional 和 additional 一样以 -al 结尾：optional extra 就是你可以“加”的那一项。

abstract.en: An option is the smallest unit of freedom: a real alternative that you can still take.
abstract.cn: 选项是自由的最小单位：一个你仍然拿得走的真实备选。

abstract.en: Every option is a road not yet walked; choosing burns the other roads for this trip.
abstract.cn: 每个选项都是一条尚未走过的路；一旦选择，这一趟的其他路就被烧掉了。

abstract.en: A financial option puts a price on possibility itself: you pay to keep a choice alive.
abstract.cn: 金融期权给“可能性”本身标了价：你付钱，只为让一个选择继续活着。

examples.en: The report lists several options for cutting costs, but none is painless.
examples.cn: 报告列出了几种削减成本的选项，但没有一种是轻松的。

examples.en: You always have the option to say no.
examples.cn: 你始终拥有拒绝的选项。

examples.en: The software hides advanced options unless you open the settings panel.
examples.cn: 除非打开设置面板，否则软件会隐藏高级选项。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 opt- 记成“伸手抓取”，-ion 记成“动作”：抓取的动作就是选择。
dict_mnemonic.text: opt（抓取、选择）+ -ion（名词）→ 选择、选项、选择权

root: 拉丁 optare“希望、选择”→ optio“选择”→ 法语 option → 英语 option；更早的原始印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from 'a thing you may pick' to 'the right to pick', then to priced choices (features, stock, contracts), and finally to a live choice inside a game, a program, or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“可供挑选的事物”走到“挑选的权利”，再到被标价的选择（选装配置、股票、合约），最后落到比赛、程序与计划中仍然敞开的那一次选择。

core.en: An open hand above several alternatives, ready to lift one
core.cn: 悬在几个备选之上的手，随时准备拿起一个

branches.en: Concrete alternatives: one item on a list of things you may pick.
branches.cn: 具体备选：可供挑选的清单上的一项。

branches.en: Freedom kept open: the chooser's liberty, or the deliberate refusal to commit.
branches.cn: 被保留的自由：选择者的权利，或有意不作承诺。

branches.en: Choices sold as goods: an add-on feature or a stock option.
branches.cn: 作为商品出售的选择：选装配置或股票期权。

branches.en: Choices inside a system: a football play or a software flag.
branches.cn: 系统内部的选择：橄榄球战术或软件开关。

branches.en: The paid right: liberty turned into a priced, time-limited contract.
branches.cn: 付费的权利：自由变成有价格、有期限的合约。

intro.en: The opt- family is small but busy: a verb of choosing, a noun of choice, and adjectives that mark whether something is left to the chooser.
intro.cn: opt- 词族不大但很活跃：一个“选择”动词、一个“选择”名词，以及标记“是否交由选择者决定”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare 'to wish, choose' yields optio 'choice' and the adjective optativus 'expressing a wish'. English opt is a back-formation from option.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare“希望、选择”产生 optio“选择”和形容词 optativus“表达愿望的”。英语的 opt 是从 option 逆构出来的动词。

items.meaning: the act or right of choosing; a thing chosen
items.meaningCN: 选择的行为或权利；被选中的事物
items.example: You have the option to decline.

items.meaning: in a way that is not required
items.example: The form can optionally include a photo.
items.exampleCN: 表格可以选择附上一张照片。

items.meaning: to choose or decide between alternatives
items.example: Most students opt for the shorter course.
items.exampleCN: 大多数学生选择较短的那门课。

items.meaning: a choice to leave or not take part
items.example: The newsletter uses an opt-out system.
items.exampleCN: 这份通讯采用“默认订阅、可退出”的机制。

items.meaning: a choice to join or take part
items.exampleCN: 营销邮件需要用户主动选择加入的同意。

items.meaning: to choose for oneself and take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 采纳；收养（选择过来成为自己的）
items.example: The school adopted a new reading method.
items.exampleCN: 学校采纳了一种新的阅读教学法。

items.meaning: the act of taking something as one's own
items.example: The adoption of the plan took two years.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划的采纳用了两年。

items.meaning: expressing a wish, as a grammatical mood
items.example: Ancient Greek has an optative mood.

definition_en: not required, but left to a person's own choice; offered as an extra that may be taken or left
core_image: 一张报名表上，几行字旁印着小星号，其余空格留白等人自行决定
scene: 报名表摊在桌上，几行字旁印着小小的星号，其余空格留白，等人自己决定填不填。The extra lesson is optional, so nobody has to stay after class.

senses.title: Not required but allowed
senses.definition: available to be done or taken if one wishes, but not demanded by any rule
senses.definitionCN: 想做或想取用便可做、可取用，但并不由任何规则强制要求
senses.example: Attendance at the evening talk is optional.
senses.exampleCN: 晚上的讲座可以自愿参加。
senses.why: Latin optio named a choice, so the adjective simply marks something that sits among options rather than among duties.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 optio 指「选择」，所以这个形容词只是标明某事列在选项之中，而不在义务之列；重点落在「可以挑」。

senses.title: Offered as an extra that may be added
senses.titleCN: 作为额外附加、可加可不加的
senses.definition: supplied in addition to what is basic or necessary, so that a person may add it or leave it out
senses.definitionCN: 在基本或必需的内容之外额外提供，可以添上，也可以略去
senses.example: The suitcase comes with an optional strap for long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子配有一条可选背带，走远路时可以用。
senses.why: Once a thing is one of the options, it can be offered beside the main item, and the word shifts from permission to a purchasable extra.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然位列选项，就可以摆在主件旁边额外提供，词义便从「允许」转到「可添置的附加项」，决定权仍在使用者手里。

senses.title: Chosen rather than compulsory, of a school subject
senses.definition: describing a course or subject that a student may choose instead of a required one
senses.definitionCN: 形容学生可以自行选择、而非必修的课程或科目
senses.example: She took two optional courses in her second year.
senses.exampleCN: 她在二年级选了两门选修课。
senses.why: In a curriculum the choice becomes visible as a list of subjects, and optional marks the ones a student may pick up or pass by.
senses.whyCN: 在课程表里，「选择」变成一张科目清单，optional 标出那些可以选上、也可以略过的科目；这是选择在教育场景中的具体落点。

intro.en: Optional is option plus the adjective ending -al; option goes back through French to a Latin noun for choice.
intro.cn: optional 是 option 加形容词词尾 -al；option 则经法语上溯到表示「选择」的拉丁名词。

items.en: Optio meant a choice or the power of choosing, and it could also name a person chosen for a duty.
items.cn: optio 指选择或选择权，也可指被选出来担任某项事务的人。

items.en: The verb optare meant to choose or to wish, and it stands behind the whole English family.
items.cn: 动词 optare 意为选择、盼望，是整个英语词族的源头。

items.en: Old French option kept the sense of a choice between possibilities and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 option 保留「在多种可能中作选择」的意思，并传入英语。

items.en: English took option as a noun of choice, and by the seventeenth century optional marked what was left to choice.
items.cn: 英语以 option 作表示选择的名词，到十七世纪 optional 用来标明「交由选择决定」的事物。

items.en: Modern English uses optional for forms, features, courses and extras that nobody is obliged to take.
items.cn: 现代英语用 optional 指表格项、功能、课程与附加物中无人必须接受的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for choosing and a spelling that only resembles them; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is left to free will.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「选择」词根上的词，以及只是拼写相近的一个词；近义组收表示「交由自由意愿」的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a choice-noun wearing an adjective ending, so its hooks all turn on who holds the decision.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是穿着形容词词尾的「选择」名词，记忆钩子都围绕「决定权在谁手里」。

normal.en: Option means a choice, and optional adds -al, so the word describes what choice is allowed to reach.
normal.cn: option 意为选择，optional 加 -al，所以这个词描述的是「选择所能触及的范围」。

normal.en: The ending -al turns a noun of choice into an adjective of permission rather than of command.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 把表示选择的名词变成表示许可的形容词，而不是表示命令的形容词。

normal.en: Optional course and optional extra follow the same logic: the item is there, but the decision is yours.
normal.cn: optional course 与 optional extra 逻辑相同：东西摆在那里，决定权归你。

normal.en: English often adds entirely to optional to stress that no hidden rule stands behind the offer.
normal.cn: 英语常在 optional 前加 entirely，强调这份好意背后没有藏着任何硬性规定。

normal.en: Optional does not mean unimportant; it means not required, and the difference is worth keeping.
normal.cn: optional 不等于不重要，它只表示不作要求，这个区别值得守住。

abstract.en: An asterisk beside a line on a form is a small sign that says this blank is yours to fill or leave.
abstract.cn: 表格行旁的小星号是个小小提示：这一格填或不填都由你。

abstract.en: A menu with a page of add-ons keeps the meal complete without them, and optional is that extra page.
abstract.cn: 一份另附加页的菜单，不加也吃得完整，optional 就是那页附加内容。

abstract.en: A path that splits, one side marked required and one side open, is the word drawn as a choice on the ground.

definition_zh: 口头的；口部的；口服的；口试
definition_en: spoken rather than written, or relating to the mouth; as a noun, an examination in which answers are spoken
core_image: 两个人面对面坐着，声音从嘴里出来，桌上没有纸笔
scene: 面试的小房间里，考官只开口提问，桌上没有纸笔，考生只能凭说话作答。The final exam includes an oral test that lasts ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 oral 是「口试」（第 4 个义项：以口头问答进行的考试）；句意为期末考试含一场十分钟的口试，画面是没有纸笔的小房间与面对面的两个人。

derivatives.zh: 由 oral 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「口头地；经口地」
由 oral 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「口头性；口述传统」
由 oral 加表示「主义、方法」的后缀 -ism 构成，义为「口语法；口语教学法」

senses.title: Spoken rather than written
senses.definition: expressed by speaking rather than by writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过说话表达，而非通过书写
senses.example: The company gave only an oral warning, with nothing in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 公司只作了口头警告，没有留下任何书面内容。
senses.why: Latin os, genitive oris, meant mouth, so what is oral comes out of the mouth rather than off the page.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 os（属格 oris）指「嘴」，所以 oral 的事物是从嘴里出来的，而不是从纸面来的；「口头」这一层直接由「嘴」引出。

senses.title: Relating to the mouth
senses.definition: relating to the mouth as a part of the body or to care of it
senses.definitionCN: 与作为身体部位的嘴有关，或与口腔护理有关
senses.example: Good oral hygiene protects the teeth and gums.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的口腔卫生保护牙齿与牙龈。
senses.why: The same body part that produces speech also needs care, so the word keeps the plain anatomical sense beside the speaking one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个身体部位既发出话语，也需要被照料，所以这个词在「说话」之外保留了朴素的解剖义；这是词根本义的直接延伸。

senses.title: Taken by mouth, of medicine
senses.definition: of a medicine, taken through the mouth rather than injected or applied to the skin
senses.definitionCN: 指药物经口服用，而不是注射或涂在皮肤上
senses.example: The doctor changed her to an oral antibiotic.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给她换成了口服抗生素。
senses.why: Because the mouth is the entrance to the body, a remedy swallowed through it is named with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 嘴是身体的一个入口，所以经口吞下的药也用同一个形容词来命名；「口部」的空间意义由此转成了用药途径。

senses.title: A spoken examination
senses.definition: an examination in which a candidate answers questions by speaking rather than by writing
senses.definitionCN: 考生以口头回答、而非笔试作答的考试
senses.example: She passed the oral and moved on to the written part.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过了口试，接着进入笔试部分。
senses.why: When the adjective names the spoken form, it can stand alone as a noun for the spoken test itself.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词指明「口头的形式」，它就能单独作名词，指口头形式的考试本身；这是省略所修饰名词之后的形容词名词化。

intro.en: Oral comes from the Latin word for mouth and its adjective oralis; the sense of speech grew out of that plain bodily meaning.
intro.cn: oral 出自拉丁语中表示「嘴」的词及其形容词 oralis；「口头」的意思是从这个朴素的身体义长出来的。

items.en: The Latin noun os meant mouth, and its genitive stem or- is the part that reached later words.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 os 意为「嘴」，其属格词干 or- 进入了后来的词。

items.en: Oralis was formed on that stem to mean of the mouth, a plain adjective of the body.
items.cn: oralis 在这一词干上构成，意为「口的」，本是一个朴素的身体形容词。

items.en: French oral carried both the anatomical sense and the sense of what is spoken rather than written.
items.cn: 法语 oral 兼有解剖义与「说而非写」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed oral for things of the mouth, and the spoken sense grew beside it in learned and legal use.
items.cn: 英语借入 oral 指与嘴有关的事物，「口头的」这层意思在学术与法律用法中随之生长。

items.en: Modern English uses oral for speech, for mouth care, for medicine taken by mouth, and for the spoken test.
items.cn: 现代英语用 oral 指口头表达、口腔护理、口服药物，以及口头进行的考试。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin mouth-stem and two words that only resemble them in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for speech and for a spoken test.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「嘴」词干上的形式，以及两个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示言语与口头考试的词。

entries.definition: In speech, or through the mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 以口头方式，或经口地。

entries.definition: An opening or hole, especially one in the body, built from the Latin mouth-word and the verb to make.
entries.definitionCN: 开口；孔洞，尤指身体上的孔口，由拉丁语「嘴」与「做」的动词构成。

entries.definition: A skilled public speaker; the spelling resembles oral, but the word comes from Latin orare, to speak, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 擅长公开演说的人；拼写与 oral 相近，但词源是拉丁语 orare（说话），只是拼写相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: A formal speech given on an important occasion; it shares the speaking root of orator, not the mouth root of oral.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要场合发表的正式演说；它与 orator 同出「说话」词根，而非 oral 的「嘴」词根。

entries.definition: Expressed in speech rather than in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 以说话而非书写表达的。

entries.definition: Relating to words, especially to speech rather than writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与词语有关的，尤指口头而非书面的。

entries.definition: An oral examination, especially one held in a university.
entries.definitionCN: 口试，尤指大学里的口头答辩。

normalIntro.en: The word grows straight out of the Latin mouth, and its family keeps returning to the body, to speech and to the test taken by voice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词直接从拉丁语「嘴」长出来，同族用法反复回到身体、言语与以声音作答的考试。

normal.en: Os and its genitive oris mean mouth, and oralis adds -alis, so oral is an adjective laid directly on the body part.
normal.cn: os 及其属格 oris 意为「嘴」，oralis 再加 -alis，所以 oral 是直接加在身体部位上的形容词。

normal.en: The same mouth-root gives orifice, an opening, because a mouth is a hole in the body.
normal.cn: 同一「嘴」词根还给出 orifice（开口），因为嘴就是身体上的一个孔。

normal.en: Orator looks close but comes from orare, to speak, so the likeness is spelling rather than a shared root.
normal.cn: orator 看起来相近，却出自 orare（说话），所以相似处是拼写，而不是同一词根。

normal.en: Oral history and oral tradition keep the spoken sense, where words live in voices rather than on paper.
normal.cn: oral history 与 oral tradition 保留口头义，在那里话语活在声音里，而不在纸上。

normal.en: In medicine oral marks the route through the mouth, and in school it marks the spoken test, both still anchored to the body.
normal.cn: 医学里 oral 标出经口途径，学校里 oral 标出用口作答的考试，两处都仍锚定在身体上。

abstract.en: A small room with two chairs, no paper and no pens, is the word oral reduced to its scene.
abstract.cn: 一间只摆两把椅子的小屋，没有纸也没有笔，就是把 oral 还原成场景。

abstract.en: A spoon of syrup going in through the mouth shows the body used as a doorway, which is the medical sense of the word.
abstract.cn: 一勺糖浆从嘴里送进去，显示身体被当作一道门，这就是这个词的医学义。

abstract.en: A student answers aloud while an examiner listens, and the spoken answer becomes the exam itself.
abstract.cn: 学生出声作答、考官在旁倾听，口头的回答于是变成了考试本身。

examples.en: The final exam includes an oral test that lasts ten minutes.
examples.cn: 期末考试含一场十分钟的口试。

examples.en: The company gave only an oral warning, with nothing in writing.
examples.cn: 公司只作了口头警告，没有留下任何书面内容。

examples.en: Good oral hygiene protects the teeth and gums.
examples.cn: 良好的口腔卫生保护牙齿与牙龈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，若」——只在嘴上说、不动笔；oral 意为口头的。

root: 拉丁语 os（属格 oris，嘴）→ 晚期拉丁 oralis（口的）→ 法语 oral → 英语 oral；由「嘴」引申为「口头的」，再作名词指口试。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mouth; the senses spread from what the mouth produces in speech, to care of the mouth, to medicine taken through it, to the spoken test.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「嘴」；义项从嘴在言语中产生的东西，扩展到口腔的照料、经口服下的药，再到以口作答的考试。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people facing each other, words leaving the mouth, no paper on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人面对面，话从嘴里出来，桌上没有纸笔。

branches.en: an interview room with no paper and no pens
branches.cn: 没有纸笔的面试小房间

branches.en: a doctor looking into a patient's mouth
branches.cn: 医生查看病人的口腔

branches.cn: 一勺经口服下的糖浆

branches.en: a student answering aloud while an examiner listens
branches.cn: 学生出声作答，考官倾听

branches.en: the same spoken act, once as a warning and once as a test
branches.cn: 同一种口头行为，一次是警告，一次是考试

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun for mouth, its genitive stem, a late adjective, and two English endings that make the adverb and the noun-like form.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「嘴」的名词、它的属格词干、一个晚期形容词，以及两个构成副词与类名词形式的英语词尾。

definition_zh: 轨道；绕行；（影响、势力）范围；眼窝；原子轨道
definition_en: the curved path of one body around another, or to move along such a path
core_image: 孩子甩着一根系绳的小球，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转，绳在空气里拉出圆的痕迹
scene: 操场边的孩子把一只系绳的小球甩起来，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转。The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 orbit 指「一个物体绕另一个物体运行的路径」（第 1 个义项：绕行的曲线路径）；句意为孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。图中可辨识物件：系绳小球、握绳的手、圆形痕迹、操场地面、孩子背影；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 轨道；势力范围；眼窝；（物理）原子轨道

senses.title: A path around a body
senses.definition: the curved path of a body around a more massive one under gravity
senses.definitionCN: 在引力作用下，一个天体绕更大质量天体的弯曲路径
senses.example: The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。
senses.why: the word began as the rut of a wheel, so the earliest idea is a track that something follows rather than a force that pulls it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指车轮的辙，因此最早的想法是某物沿着走的轨迹，而非拉着它的力。

senses.title: To move along that path
senses.definition: to travel around a body in a closed or repeating path
senses.definitionCN: 沿闭合或重复的路径绕某天体运行
senses.example: The station orbits the earth once every ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 空间站每九十分钟绕地球一圈。
senses.why: once the noun meant a track, the verb could mean travelling on it, and English formed it without adding any new root.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词意为轨迹，动词自然可意为沿轨迹行进，英语无需另加词根就构成了它。

senses.title: One complete circuit
senses.definition: one completed trip around a body, used as a unit of time or counting
senses.definitionCN: 绕某天体完整走完的一圈，用作计时或计数的单位
senses.example: The satellite completed its thousandth orbit this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗卫星今早完成了第千圈绕行。
senses.why: a closed path can be counted, so the same noun measures repetition rather than only geometry.
senses.whyCN: 闭合路径可以计数，因此同一个名词也度量重复次数，而不只度量几何。

senses.title: An electron's orbital
senses.titleCN: 物理与化学中的原子轨道
senses.definition: in physics and chemistry, a region where an electron is likely to be found around a nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 物理与化学中指电子在核周围出现的概率区域
senses.example: The first shell holds one spherical orbital.
senses.exampleCN: 第一层只有一个球形轨道。
senses.why: early models pictured electrons circling like planets, and the word survived after the picture became a probability cloud.
senses.whyCN: 早期模型把电子想成像行星一样绕行，而在这个图像变成概率云之后，这个词仍留了下来。

senses.title: The eye socket
senses.definition: the bony cavity that holds the eye
senses.definitionCN: 容纳眼球的骨质腔
senses.example: A blow near the orbit can damage the eye itself.
senses.exampleCN: 眼窝附近的打击可能伤到眼睛本身。
senses.why: the socket is a ring-shaped hollow, and Latin used the same wheel-track word for it, so English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 眼窝是环形的凹处，拉丁语用同一个「车辙」词指它，因此英语保留了两义。

senses.title: A sphere of influence
senses.definition: the range within which a person, country or idea exerts influence
senses.definitionCN: 一个人、国家或观念施加影响的范围
senses.example: Smaller states moved into the larger neighbour's orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的国家进入了更大邻国的影响圈。
senses.why: bodies near a massive one are held by it, so politics borrowed the picture for clients held by a power.
senses.whyCN: 靠近大质量天体的物体会被它牵住，因此政治借这幅图景指被某个强国牵住的附庸。

senses.title: Going into orbit
senses.definition: used of spacecraft reaching and staying in a path around a body
senses.definitionCN: 指航天器抵达并停留在绕某天体的路径上
senses.example: The rocket put the weather satellite into orbit within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭在一小时内把气象卫星送入轨道。
senses.why: spaceflight made the phrase everyday, and 'into orbit' became a fixed way to describe a successful launch.
senses.whyCN: 航天让这个短语变得日常，「进入轨道」成了描述发射成功的固定说法。

senses.title: Going round the same subject
senses.titleCN: 比喻：绕着同一个问题打转
senses.definition: figuratively, to keep returning to one topic without settling it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻反复回到同一个话题却始终不解决
senses.example: The meeting orbited the budget question for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议绕着预算问题转了整整两小时。
senses.why: an orbit returns to the same point, so the metaphor describes discussion that moves but never arrives.
senses.whyCN: 轨道会回到同一点，因此这个比喻形容讨论在动却始终不到达。

senses.title: Named orbital regimes
senses.titleCN: 按高度命名的轨道类型
senses.definition: used in fixed names such as low Earth orbit, polar orbit and geostationary orbit
senses.definitionCN: 用于近地轨道、极轨道、地球静止轨道等固定名称
senses.example: Most communication satellites sit in geostationary orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 多数通信卫星位于地球静止轨道。
senses.why: each regime has different uses, so the noun became part of technical labels that say where a satellite works.
senses.whyCN: 各轨道区间用途不同，因此这个名词成为说明卫星工作位置的技术标签的一部分。

intro.en: Orbit comes from Latin orbita 'wheel-rut, track', from orbis 'circle, disk'. English first used it for the eye socket and only later for a heavenly path. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbit 来自拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」，其源为 orbis「圆、盘」。英语最早用它指眼窝，后来才指天体路径。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita was the rut a wheel leaves, and by extension any beaten track or course.
items.cn: orbita 是车轮留下的辙，引申为任何被踩出的轨迹或行程。

items.en: Orbis meant a circle, a disk or the round world; the track word was built from it.
items.cn: orbis 意为圆、盘或圆形的世界；轨迹一词即由它构成。

items.en: English orbit first named the bony ring around the eye, a sense Latin already had.
items.cn: 英语 orbit 最早指眼周的骨环，这一义拉丁语已有。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy applied the same word to the path of a body, since both are enclosing tracks.
items.cn: 17 世纪天文学把同一个词用于天体路径，因为两者都是围合的轨迹。

items.en: The twentieth century made 'into orbit' a household phrase and added named regimes such as low Earth orbit.
items.cn: 20 世纪使「进入轨道」成为家常用语，并增添了近地轨道等命名区间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of orbis is not established, and any older Indo-European form suggested for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：orbis 在拉丁语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the derived forms that are easily swapped; group two holds words for a route or a turn.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混用的派生形式；第二组是表示路线或一圈的词。

entries.definitionCN: 轨道的；化学中也作名词指电子的概率区域。

entries.definition: The present participle, used for something currently in orbit rather than for the path itself.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，指当前正在轨运行的事物，而非路径本身。

entries.definition: A spacecraft designed to circle a body; the -er suffix marks the agent, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 设计用来绕某天体飞行的航天器；-er 后缀标记执行者，而非路径。

entries.definition: A sphere or globe, from the same orbis; it names the round thing, not the track around it.
entries.definitionCN: 球体或圆球，同出 orbis；它命名圆的东西，而非绕它的轨迹。

entries.definition: The path of a moving body, often one that does not repeat; an orbit is the repeating case.
entries.definitionCN: 运动天体的路径，常指不重复者；轨道是其中重复的情形。

entries.definition: A single circling; it names the motion, while orbit names the track.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行一圈；它命名运动，而 orbit 命名轨迹。

entries.definition: A perfectly round curve; orbits are usually ellipses, so circle is only the special case.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的圆形曲线；轨道通常是椭圆，圆只是特例。

entries.definition: The extent something can reach; it overlaps the 'sphere of influence' sense but has no orbital image.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所能达到的范围；与「势力范围」义重叠，但没有轨道意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relations, real compounds and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词族关系、真实搭配与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin orbita 'wheel-rut': the path is a groove in space.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbita「车辙」：路径是空间中磨出的沟。

normal.en: English used orbit for the eye socket before it used it for the moon.
normal.cn: 英语先用 orbit 指眼窝，后来才用它指月球。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiting, orbiter, orbit insertion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiting、orbiter、orbit insertion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark spaceflight: go into orbit, low Earth orbit, geostationary orbit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标记航天：进入轨道、近地轨道、地球静止轨道。

normal.en: The electron sense survives in chemistry as the orbital.
normal.cn: 电子义在化学中以 orbital 的形式留存。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that keeps circling a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话老绕着一扇锁着的门打转。

abstract.en: Picture a small country held in the gravity of a large one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小国被大国的引力牵住。

abstract.en: Picture a stone skipping around a whirlpool instead of falling in.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子绕着旋涡转，而没有掉进去。

examples.en: The moon's orbit is tilted about five degrees from the ecliptic.
examples.cn: 月球轨道相对黄道倾斜约五度。

examples.en: Engineers raised the satellite's orbit to extend its life.
examples.cn: 工程师抬高了卫星轨道以延长其寿命。

examples.en: The discussion orbited the same objection all afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午的讨论都绕着同一个反对意见打转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比它（orbit）」——哦，它又比它多绕了一圈 → 轨道、绕行

root: 拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」← orbis「圆、盘」；英语先指眼窝，17 世纪起指天体路径。orbis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the track to the act of following it, to one turn, to an electron's cloud, an eye socket, a sphere of influence, a launch, a metaphor and named orbital zones.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从轨迹出发，到沿轨迹行进、一整圈、电子的云、眼窝、势力范围、一次发射、一个比喻，最后到按高度命名的轨道区间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a string, circling a hand and leaving a ring in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只系绳的小球绕手转，在空气里留下一圈痕迹。

branches.en: MOTION AND COUNT: travelling on the path, and one completed lap.
branches.cn: 运动与计数：沿路径行进，以及走完一圈。

branches.en: RINGS AT SMALL SCALE: electron clouds and eye sockets repeat the enclosing circle.
branches.cn: 小尺度的环：电子云与眼窝重复了围合的圆圈。

branches.en: HELD IN PLACE: politics and argument both describe bodies that cannot leave a centre.
branches.cn: 被牵在原处：政治与争论都描述离不开中心的东西。

branches.en: ENGINEERED ORBITS: launches and named regimes turn the path into a destination.
branches.cn: 被工程化的轨道：发射与命名区间把路径变成目的地。

branches.en: ROOT IMAGE: the wheel-rut is the whole family's source.
branches.cn: 根源意象：车辙是整个词族的来源。

intro.en: Orbit is a Latin noun with a small English family built by suffixes for relation, action and agent.
intro.cn: orbit 是一个拉丁名词，英语用表示关系、动作与执行者的后缀构建了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita 'track' and orbis 'circle' supply orbit and orb; the family has no Greek element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbis「圆」提供 orbit 与 orb；这个词族不含希腊成分。

items.example: The Latin word is the direct source of orbit.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词是 orbit 的直接来源。

items.example: The probe orbited the planet for a year.
items.exampleCN: 探测器绕这颗行星运行了一年。
一座在轨实验室从头顶经过。

items.example: The orbiter mapped the surface for years.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器测绘地表多年。

latinEntries.meaning: the circle of lands, the whole world

definition_zh: 管弦乐队；乐池；正厅前排座位；歌队场地
definition_en: a large group of musicians playing together on strings, woodwind, brass and percussion, and also the space in a theatre where they sit or the seats nearest that space
core_image: 乐池的暗处，一排琴弓同时抬起，等舞台上第一束光落下
scene: 开演前的剧场里，观众还在找座位，乐池的灯先亮了起来，提琴手们把弓一根根试过。The orchestra tuned slowly while the audience settled in.
sceneCN: 这里是「管弦乐队」（第 1 个义项：在乐池里一起演奏的乐手团体）；句意为观众陆续坐定时，乐队慢慢把音调准。图中可辨识物件：乐池灯、琴弓、乐谱架。

pos.zh: 管弦乐队；乐池；正厅前排座位；歌队场地

derivatives.zh: 由 orchestra 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「管弦乐队的；管弦乐的」
由 orchestra 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「把……编配成管弦乐；精心安排」
由 orchestrate 加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「配器；精心编排」

senses.title: A large group of musicians playing together
senses.definition: a large group of musicians, with strings and usually woodwind, brass and percussion, who perform music as one body
senses.definitionCN: 由弦乐等多组乐手组成、作为一个整体演奏的大型乐队
senses.example: The orchestra rehearsed the new symphony twice.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队把这部新交响曲排练了两遍。
senses.why: Greek orchestra named the place where the chorus danced; by the seventeenth century the musicians working in that place took the name, and the group outlived the room.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 orchestra 本指歌队起舞的场地；到十七世纪，在那个场地里奏乐的人反过来用这个词称呼自己，最后留在语言里的是团体，而不是那间屋子。

senses.title: The space where the players sit
senses.definition: the area in front of and usually below the stage where the musicians sit during a performance
senses.definitionCN: 舞台上及其前方、通常低下去的一块区域，演出时乐手坐在那里
senses.example: The violins were already in the orchestra when the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起时，小提琴手已经在乐池里就位。
senses.why: The word started life as the name of a space, and English kept that sense for the part of a theatre reserved for players, now often carried by the fuller phrase orchestra pit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就是一块场地的名字，英语一直保留「剧场里留给乐手的那块地方」这层含义，如今多由更完整的 orchestra pit 承担。

senses.title: The front seats on the main floor
senses.definition: the seats on the main floor of a theatre, especially the front part, as opposed to the balcony
senses.definitionCN: 剧场底层、尤其靠前区域的座位，与楼座相对
senses.example: We booked two seats in the orchestra for the opening night.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜我们订了两个正厅前排座位。
senses.why: In American theatres the floor area nearest the stage kept the old name of the space, so a ticket can be in the orchestra with no musician involved.
senses.whyCN: 在美国的剧场里，最靠近舞台的底层区域沿用了这块场地的旧名，于是一张票可以写作「in the orchestra」，而整句话和乐手毫无关系。

senses.title: The dancing floor of a Greek theatre
senses.definition: the circular area in front of the stage in an ancient Greek theatre, where the chorus sang and danced
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊剧场中舞台前供歌队歌唱、起舞的圆形场地
senses.example: Archaeologists traced the stone edge of the orchestra at the old theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 考古人员在老剧场里辨认出了歌队场地的石砌边缘。
senses.why: The original Greek word named exactly this dancing floor, so the oldest recorded sense of the English word is a piece of architecture rather than a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词指的正是这块起舞的场地，所以英语这个词最早记下的含义是一处建筑空间，而不是一群人。

intro.en: Orchestra is a Greek word for a dancing floor that reached English through Latin and the Renaissance study of ancient theatre.
intro.cn: orchestra 是希腊语中表示「起舞场地」的词，经拉丁语与文艺复兴时期对古剧场的研读进入英语。

items.en: The Greek verb orkheisthai meant to dance, and the noun orchestra named the place where the chorus danced in front of the stage.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 orkheisthai 意为跳舞，名词 orchestra 指舞台前歌队起舞的地方。

items.en: In the theatre of Athens the orchestra was the circular floor between the audience and the stage, entered and used by the chorus.
items.cn: 在雅典的剧场中，orchestra 是观众与舞台之间那块圆形地面，歌队由此进出并使用。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for the same part of a Roman theatre, where the seats nearest the stage were later reserved for senators.
items.cn: 拉丁语借来这个希腊词，指罗马剧场中的同一区域，靠近舞台的座位后来留给元老。

items.en: English writers took the word from Latin for the space before the stage, and then transferred it to the musicians who played in that space.
items.cn: 十七世纪的英语作者从拉丁语借来这个词，先指舞台前的空间，随后把它转给在那里奏乐的乐手。

items.en: Modern English made the group of players the main sense and kept the older spatial senses in orchestra pit and orchestra seats.
items.cn: 现代英语把「演奏团体」定为主要含义，同时把较老的空间含义留在 orchestra pit 与 orchestra seats 里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the orchestral family built on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for groups that make music.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词干长出的乐队词族；近义组收其他表示「一起奏乐的团体」的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to an orchestra or to music written for one.
entries.definitionCN: 与管弦乐队有关的，或为乐队写的。

entries.definition: To arrange a piece of music for an orchestra, or to plan something carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队配器，或精心安排一件事。

entries.definition: The art of writing music for an orchestra, or a carefully arranged plan.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队写作的技艺，或精心编排的方案。

entries.definition: A group of musicians or performers who work as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个整体演出的乐手或演员团体。

entries.definition: A large work for orchestra, or an orchestra that plays such works.
entries.definitionCN: 为管弦乐队写的大型作品，或演奏这类作品的乐团。

entries.definition: A smaller group of players, often with drums and brass.
entries.definitionCN: 人数较少、常含鼓与铜管的乐队。

normalIntro.en: Every form in this entry grows from a Greek word for a dancing floor, so the mnemonics move between the room and the people who fill it.
normalIntro.cn: 这一条里所有形式都长自希腊语中「起舞场地」这个词，联想便在房间和填满它的人之间来回。

normal.en: Orchestra began as a Greek word for a dancing floor, so the oldest picture in it is feet moving on stone.
normal.cn: orchestra 最初是希腊语里「起舞场地」的说法，所以它最老的画面是石地上走动的脚步。

normal.en: The name then moved from the floor to the players standing on it.
normal.cn: 这个名字随后从场地挪到站在场地上的乐手身上。

normal.en: Orchestra pit keeps the old room sense, while orchestra alone now usually means the group.
normal.cn: orchestra pit 保留了「房间」旧义，而单独用的 orchestra 现在通常指团体。

normal.en: Orchestral adds -al and turns the players into an adjective.
normal.cn: orchestral 加 -al，把乐手团体变成形容词。

normal.en: Orchestrate adds -ate and turns arranging for that group into a verb.
normal.cn: orchestrate 加 -ate，把为这个团体配器变成动词。

abstract.en: A hall dark except for the pit, where many pairs of hands move as one.
abstract.cn: 大厅全暗，只有乐池亮着，许多双手在那里合成一个动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a floor now means the people who make the floor noisy.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指地板的词，现在指把地板弄得热闹起来的那群人。

abstract.en: The room is small, but what it sends into the hall is larger than the room.
abstract.cn: 那间屋子很小，可它送进大厅的声音比屋子大得多。

examples.en: The orchestra rehearsed the new symphony twice.
examples.cn: 乐队把这部新交响曲排练了两遍。

examples.en: The violins were already in the orchestra when the curtain rose.
examples.cn: 幕布升起时，小提琴手已经在乐池里就位。

examples.en: We booked two seats in the orchestra for the opening night.
examples.cn: 首演之夜我们订了两个正厅前排座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥凯斯特拉」——一群人挤在台下那块小地方，节拍一起走；记住 orchestra 是管弦乐队。

root: 希腊语 ὀρχήστρα（歌队起舞的场地）源自 ὀρχεῖσθαι（跳舞），经拉丁语 orchestra 进入英语；词义从场地转到在场地上奏乐的团体。拉丁语 orchestra 本身也只是借自希腊语，并非独立的同族词，因此不列拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place where people make music together; the senses run from that room to the players, to the seats, and back to the ancient dancing floor.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「人们一起奏乐的那块地方」；义项从这块地方走到人，再到座位，最后回到古代那块起舞的场地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bows lifted together in the dark of a pit.
core.cn: 核心意象：乐池的暗处，一排琴弓同时抬起。

branches.en: a conductor raising both hands before the first beat
branches.cn: 指挥在第一个拍子前抬起双手

branches.en: lamps coming on over empty music stands below the stage
branches.cn: 舞台下方空谱架上的灯亮起

branches.en: a ticket printed with a row and a seat number
branches.cn: 一张印着排号与座号的票

branches.en: chorus members circling a stone floor
branches.cn: 歌队绕着石砌地面走成圆圈

branches.en: a guide pointing to the worn edge of an ancient stage
branches.cn: 向导指着古剧场舞台磨损的边缘

intro.en: Orchestra is not built from English pieces but from a Greek noun and its verb, with later English suffixes making the adjective and the verb of arranging.
intro.cn: orchestra 不是用英语部件拼成的，而是来自一个希腊名词及其动词，后来再加英语后缀造出形容词与「配器」动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin, and Latin orchestra is itself a borrowing from Greek rather than a native cognate, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，拉丁语 orchestra 本身也是从希腊语借去的，并非本土同族词，因此不列拉丁条目。

place or instrument of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作的场所或工具

items.meaning: the same space in a Roman theatre
items.meaningCN: 罗马剧场中的同一区域

items.meaning: a group of musicians, or the space they use
to arrange music for an orchestra, or to plan something
items.meaningCN: 为管弦乐队配器；精心安排

definition_zh: 顺序；次序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；秩序；修会；勋章；议事规则
definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章

derivatives.zh: 有序的；被命令的
整齐的；勤务兵
排序；次序安排

普通的（同出拉丁 ordo 词根）
